elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 我们可以认为人乳头瘤病毒和Epstein-Barr病毒是乳腺癌的重要危险因素;然而,需要进行研究来阐明这些病毒在疾病发展中的作用。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能为未来关于 人乳头瘤病毒 在乳腺癌发展中的作用的研究提供信息,并强调需要进一步研究以阐明其对该疾病的潜在贡献。

title: Human Papillomavirus DNA Detection in Laryngeal Squamous Cell Carcinoma: Prevalence and Exploratory Survival Associations in a Retrospective Cohort from the Mexican Bajío Region
abstract: Background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a well-established etiological and prognostic factor in oropharyngeal cancer, but its role in laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) remains controversial. Objective: To estimate the prevalence of HPV DNA in LSCC and to analyze its association with clinicopathological characteristics and survival. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 47 consecutive patients with histologically confirmed LSCC diagnosed between June 2007 and August 2022 at a referral hospital in the Bajío region of Mexico. HPV DNA was detected by consensus PCR using GP5+/GP6+ primers; HPV genotyping and markers of viral transcriptional activity were not assessed. Overall survival (OS) and locoregional disease-free survival (locoregional DFS) were analyzed using the Kaplan–Meier method and Cox regression. Results: Most patients were men (95.7%), with a mean age of 62.5 ± 11.2 years; 74.5% were smokers, 61.7% consumed alcohol, and 63.8% (30/47) were diagnosed at stage IV. HPV DNA was detected in 6 tumors (12.8%; 95% CI 4.8–25.7). Positivity was numerically higher in glottic (28.6%) and non-keratinizing (22.2%) tumors and in stage I–II disease (33.3% vs. 7.5% in stage III–IV; p = 0.120). HPV-positive patients underwent surgery less frequently (33.3% vs. With a median follow-up of 48.7 months, the 2- and 5-year OS rates were 52.7% and 32.1%, respectively. HPV status was not associated with OS (4 deaths among the 6 HPV-positive patients; HR 1.42; 95% CI 0.48–4.15; adjusted HR 1.07; 95% CI 0.32–3.61; p = 0.918), locoregional DFS (HR 1.02), or locoregional recurrence (16.7% vs. Conclusions: Our results suggest that approximately one in eight LSCCs in this cohort harbored HPV DNA; positivity was numerically higher in earlier-stage disease. No prognostic association was detected, although statistical power was limited (minimum detectable HR ≈ 4.6) and HPV status was based on DNA detection only.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to estimate the prevalence of HPV DNA in LSCC and to analyze its association with clinicopathological characteristics and survival. HPV is a well-established etiological and prognostic factor in oropharyngeal cancer, but its role in LSCC remains controversial.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study of 47 consecutive patients with histologically confirmed LSCC diagnosed between June 2007 and August 2022 at a referral hospital in the Bajío region of Mexico was conducted.
analysis.methods: HPV DNA was detected by consensus PCR using GP5+/GP6+ primers. Overall survival (OS) and locoregional disease-free survival (locoregional DFS) were analyzed using the Kaplan–Meier method and Cox regression.
analysis.main_results: HPV DNA was detected in 6 tumors (12.8%; 95% CI 4.8–25.7). Positivity was numerically higher in glottic (28.6%) and non-keratinizing (22.2%) tumors and in stage I–II disease (33.3% vs. 7.5% in stage III–IV; p = 0.120). HPV-positive patients underwent surgery less frequently (33.3% vs. With a median follow-up of 48.7 months, the 2- and 5-year OS rates were 52.7% and 32.1%, respectively. HPV status was not associated with OS (HR 1.42; 95% CI 0.48–4.15; adjusted HR 1.07; 95% CI 0.32–3.61; p = 0.918) or locoregional DFS (HR 1.02).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The results suggest that approximately one in eight LSCCs in this cohort harbored HPV DNA; positivity was numerically higher in earlier-stage disease. No prognostic association was detected, although statistical power was limited (minimum detectable HR ≈ 4.6) and HPV status was based on DNA detection only.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings caution that HPV DNA detection alone may not be sufficient for prognostic purposes in LSCC. They suggest that HPV positivity is more common in earlier-stage disease and may have implications for surveillance and treatment strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design, small sample size, and lack of HPV genotyping and markers of viral transcriptional activity. The statistical power was limited, and the results should be interpreted with caution.

analysis.summary_en: This study estimated the prevalence of HPV DNA in LSCC and found it in 12.8% of cases. HPV positivity was higher in earlier-stage disease but not associated with survival outcomes, suggesting limited prognostic value.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估 LSCC 中 HPV DNA 的 患病率 并分析其与临床病理特征和生存的关系。HPV 是口咽癌中公认的病因和预后因素,但其在 LSCC 中的作用仍存在争议。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对 2007 年 6 月至 2022 年 8 月期间在墨西哥巴希奥地区一家转诊医院诊断的连续 47 名经组织学证实患有 LSCC 的患者进行了一项回顾性 队列研究 研究。
elements_zh.methods: 使用 GP5+/GP6+ 引物通过共有 PCR 检测 HPV DNA。使用Kaplan-Meier法和Cox回归分析总生存期(OS)和局部无病生存期(局部DFS)。

title: Association of non-16/18 high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) genotype multiplicity with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia 2+ detection in persistent HPV positivity
abstract: Objectives: To investigate the association between multiple non-16/18 high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) genotype positivity and histologically confirmed cervical intraepithelial neoplasia 2+ (CIN2+) among women undergoing colposcopic biopsy because of persistent non-16/18 high-risk HPV positivity. Material and Methods: This retrospective study evaluated 238 women aged 18–65 years who underwent colposcopic biopsy at a single center after high-risk HPV positivity on at least two consecutive tests performed 12 months or more apart. HPV16-positive and HPV18-positive women were excluded. Multiplicity was defined from the genotype categories reported on the most recent pre-colposcopy test. A post hoc parsimonious logistic regression model included multiplicity and high-risk cytology. The primary outcome was histologically confirmed CIN2+. Results: Of the 238 women, 159 had single-category positivity, and 79 had multiple-category positivity; 25 women had CIN2+. CIN2+ was detected in 14/79 women (17.7%) in the multiple HPV group and 11/159 women (6.9%) in the single HPV group. The unadjusted odds ratio (OR) was 2.90, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.25–6.72, P = 0.014. After adjustment for high-risk cytology, the estimate was attenuated and no longer statistically significant; adjusted OR 2.37, 95% CI 0.96–5.82, P = 0.061. The HPV31-containing multiple-infection subgroup finding was exploratory and not statistically significant. Conclusion: In this selected cohort with repeated non-16/18 high-risk HPV positivity, multiple reported genotype-category positivity was associated with higher unadjusted CIN2+ detection, but the estimate was attenuated after limited adjustment for high-risk cytology. The HPV31 subgroup result was preliminary and hypothesis-generating. These findings do not establish multiplicity as an independent or causal risk factor.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 旨在调查因持续非 16/18 高危型HPV 阳性而接受阴道镜活检的女性中多个非 16/18 高危 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 基因型阳性与组织学证实的宫颈上皮内瘤变 2+ (CIN2+) 之间的关联。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项回顾性研究评估了 238 名 18-65 岁的女性,她们在至少两次间隔 12 个月或更长时间的连续测试中 高危型HPV 呈阳性后,在单一中心接受了阴道镜活检。HPV16 阳性和 HPV18 阳性女性被排除在外。
elements_zh.methods: HPV 多样性是根据最近阴道镜检查前测试报告的基因型类别来定义的。事后简约逻辑回归模型包括多重性和高风险细胞学。主要结果是组织学证实的 CIN2+。
elements_zh.main_results: Of the 238 women, 159 had single-category positivity, and 79 had multiple-category positivity; 25 women had CIN2+. CIN2+ was detected in 14/79 women (17.7%) in the multiple HPV group and 11/159 women (6.9%) in the single HPV group. The unadjusted odds ratio (OR) was 2.90, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.25–6.72, P = 0.014. After adjustment for high-risk cytology, the estimate was attenuated and no longer statistically significant; adjusted OR 2.37, 95% CI 0.96–5.82, P = 0.061. The HPV31-containing multiple-infection subgroup finding was exploratory and not statistically significant.
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在这个选定的具有重复非 16/18 高危型HPV 阳性的 队列研究 中,多个报告的基因型类别阳性与较高的未调整 CIN2+ 检测相关,但在对高风险细胞学进行有限调整后,估计值有所减弱。HPV31 亚组结果是初步的且是假设性的。这些发现并未将多重性确定为独立或因果风险因素。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,非 16/18 高危型HPV 基因型的多样性可能是持续非 16/18 高危型HPV 阳性女性 CIN2+ 风险增加的标志,但需要进一步的研究来证实这种关联并了解其临床意义。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其回顾性设计和患有 CIN2+ 的女性人数较少而受到限制。高危细胞学的调整是有限的,HPV31亚组的发现是探索性的。证据强度中等。

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项回顾性研究评估了 238 名 18-65 岁的女性,她们在至少两次间隔 12 个月或更长时间的连续测试中 高危型HPV 呈阳性后,在单一中心接受了阴道镜活检。HPV16 阳性和 HPV18 阳性女性被排除在外。
analysis_zh.methods: HPV 多样性是根据最近阴道镜检查前测试报告的基因型类别来定义的。事后简约逻辑回归模型包括多重性和高风险细胞学。主要结果是组织学证实的 CIN2+。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在这个选定的具有重复非 16/18 高危型HPV 阳性的 队列研究 中,多个报告的基因型类别阳性与较高的未调整 CIN2+ 检测相关,但在对高风险细胞学进行有限调整后,估计值有所减弱。HPV31 亚组结果是初步的且是假设性的。这些发现并未将多重性确定为独立或因果风险因素。

title: A Community Engaged Feasibility Study of High-Risk Human Papillomavirus Self-Sampling for Cervical Cancer Screening in Sexual and Gender Minority People
abstract: Background and Objectives: We investigated the acceptability and feasibility of at-home self-sampling cervical cancer screening (CCS) for high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) in sexual and gender minority (SGM) Kentuckians. Methods: We conducted a descriptive qualitative study using virtual interviews to investigate socioecological factors influencing CCS and the feasibility and acceptability of at-home hrHPV self-sampling for primary CCS. Criterion and snowball sampling were used. Data were analyzed using a hybrid inductive-deductive thematic approach and team member consensus to identify salient themes. Results: Nineteen participants completed hrHPV self-sampling and qualitative interviews in 2022–2023. The 6 overarching themes identified were cervical cancer screening perceptions, prior negative healthcare experiences, desirability of hrHPV self-sampling, completing hrHPV self-sampling, concerns about hrHPV self-sampling, and reasons for study participation. Conclusion: At-home hrHPV self-sampling is a promising intervention to increase CCS in SGM people. Individuals should be reassured that self-sampling is an effective method for primary CCS and that they are likely to be able to collect a sample that will yield accurate results. To maximize the possibility of CCS completion by SGM individuals, healthcare providers and healthcare environments must be affirming, culturally competent, and informed partners throughout the CCS process.

title: Homoeopathic Management of Vulvar Genital Warts Treated with Thuja Occidentalis: A Case Report
abstract: : Vulvar genital warts, also known as condylomata acuminata, are benign epithelial proliferations of the external genitalia caused by Human Papillomavirus (HPV) infection, predominantly involving HPV types 6 and 11. A 40years old female patient presented with complaints of warts over the vulvar region for a duration of six months. On clinical examination, clustered, irregular, exophytic lesions with a rough, papillomatous surface were observed over the vulvar region. The lesions exhibited variable yellowish-white and greyish pigmentation with irregular projections, giving them a cauliflower-like appearance. Homoeopathic medicine Thuja occidentalis 200 was selected on the basis of Homoeopathic case taking and symptoms totality.
journal: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)

abstract: This systematic review evaluates the cost-effectiveness of human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination in countries of the World Health Organization (WHO) Eastern Mediterranean Region. The review aims to identify and synthesize published economic evaluations of HPV vaccination, including vaccination strategies implemented alone or in combination with cervical cancer screening. It examines reported costs, health outcomes, incremental cost-effectiveness ratios, and conclusions regarding cost-effectiveness or cost-saving. The review also describes how economic outcomes vary according to country context and vaccination programme characteristics, including vaccine price, vaccine valency, number of doses, target population, and vaccination coverage. The findings are intended to provide an overview of the available economic evidence and identify gaps requiring further country-specific research. This registration is retrospective. The review had been completed before submission of this registration; therefore, it does not constitute a prospective preregistration.

title: Meta-analysis of Epidemiological Studies on Human Papillomavirus Among Men in China
abstract: This study is a systematic review and meta-analysis aimed at comprehensively evaluating the epidemiological characteristics of Human Papillomavirus (HPV) infection among men in China. Currently, most HPV epidemiological studies in China have focused on women, and research on HPV infection in men remains insufficient, particularly regarding genotype distribution and variations across different subgroups. The primary objective of this study is to systematically estimate the overall HPV positivity rate, as well as high-risk (HR-HPV) and low-risk (LR-HPV) positivity rates among Chinese men. We will also evaluate genotype-specific positivity rates (e.g., HPV6, HPV11, HPV16, HPV52, HPV58) and conduct subgroup analyses stratified by population characteristics (e.g., men who have sex with men [MSM], patients with condyloma acuminata, outpatient clinic attendees), geographic regions, age groups, and anatomical sampling sites (e.g., anal canal, urethra, glans penis). A comprehensive literature search was performed in PubMed, Web of Science, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), and Wanfang Data from inception to February 2025. Cross-sectional studies, retrospective analyses, and cohort studies providing baseline HPV prevalence data among Chinese men will be included. Data extraction and quality assessment will be conducted independently by two reviewers. All meta-analyses will be performed using R software, applying the Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation to stabilize variances. Pooled estimates will be calculated, and heterogeneity will be assessed using the I2 statistic and chi-squared test, with subgroup analyses and sensitivity analyses (leave-one-out method) conducted to explore potential sources of heterogeneity.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本研究是一项系统回顾和荟萃分析,旨在综合评估中国男性中人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)感染的流行病学特征。

title: Vaginal microbiome alterations associated with HPV infection and cervical dysplasia in apparently healthy Togolese women
abstract: Background Persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection is the main cause of cervical cancer; however, the role of vaginal microbiome dysbiosis in HPV positivity and cervical dysplasia remains poorly characterized in sub-Saharan Africa. This study examined cervicovaginal microbiome profiles associated with HR-HPV infection and cervical dysplasia among apparently healthy women in Togo. Methods A cross-sectional, community-based cervical cancer screening study was conducted in Lomé, Togo. Vaginal dysbiosis was assessed using Nugent scoring, cervical cytology using the Bethesda 2014 system, and HR-HPV genotyping using the Anyplex II HPV HR Detection Kit. Vaginal microbiome profiling was performed by Illumina MiSeq sequencing of the V3-V4 region of the 16S rRNA gene. Bioinformatics included DADA2 for processing, phyloseq and vegan in R for diversity analyses, DESeq2 for differential abundance, and PICRUSt2 with MetaCyc for functional prediction. Results Among 338 women, HR-HPV prevalence was 31.33% and cervical dysplasia 10.06%. HPV16 was the most frequent genotype, followed by HPV51 and HPV58. HR-HPV infection and dysplasia were associated with significantly higher Nugent scores (p = 0.001 and p = 0.008). Alpha and beta diversity analyses showed no significant global microbiome restructuring by HPV or dysplasia status. However, compositional shifts showed depletion of Lactobacillus and enrichment of anaerobic and opportunistic taxa, including Atopobium vaginae, Sneathia sanguinegens, Prevotella spp., Peptostreptococcus anaerobius, and Peptoniphilus faecalis. Community state type analysis revealed a shift from Lactobacillus-dominated CSTs to dysbiotic CST IV. Functional prediction showed enrichment of sucrose degradation II, chorismate biosynthesis II, and anaerobic pathways in affected groups. No correlation was observed between HPV viral load and dysbiosis score. Conclusion HR-HPV infection and cervical dysplasia in Togolese women are linked to vaginal microbiome dysbiosis characterized by Lactobacillus depletion and enrichment of anaerobic, potentially pro-inflammatory taxa. These findings suggest a microbiome contribution to HPV positivity and cervical lesions and support its integration into prevention strategies in sub-Saharan Africa. This is the first West African community-based study combining blinded cervical screening, Nugent scoring, and sequencing-based microbiome profiling.

abstract_zh: 背景 持续高危人乳头瘤病毒(HR-HPV)感染是宫颈癌的主要原因;然而,在撒哈拉以南非洲地区,阴道微生物群失调在 HPV 阳性和宫颈发育不良中的作用仍然知之甚少。本研究调查了多哥表面健康女性中与 HR-HPV 感染和宫颈发育不良相关的宫颈阴道微生物组特征。方法 在多哥洛美进行了一项基于社区的横断面 宫颈癌 筛查研究。使用 Nugent 评分评估阴道生态失调,使用 Bethesda 2014 系统进行宫颈细胞学检查,并使用 Anyplex II HPV HR 检测试剂盒进行 HR-HPV 基因分型。通过 Illumina MiSeq 对 16S rRNA 基因的 V3-V4 区域进行测序来进行阴道微生物组分析。生物信息学包括用于处理的 DADA2、用于多样性分析的 R 中的 phyloseq 和 vegan、用于差异丰度的 DESeq2 以及用于功能预测的带有 MetaCyc 的 PICRUSt2。结果 338名女性中,HR-HPV 患病率占31.33%,宫颈发育不良占10.06%。HPV16 是最常见的基因型,其次是 HPV51 和 HPV58。HR-HPV 感染和发育异常与显着较高的 Nugent 评分相关(p = 0.001 和 p = 0.008)。Alpha 和 Beta 多样性分析显示,HPV 或不典型增生状态没有显着的全球微生物组重组。然而,成分变化表明乳酸菌减少,厌氧和机会性菌群富集,包括阴道阿托波菌、血链球菌、普雷沃氏菌、厌氧消化链球菌和粪消化链球菌。群落状态类型分析揭示了从乳酸菌主导的 CST 到菌群失调 CST IV 的转变。功能预测显示受影响组中蔗糖降解 II、分支酸生物合成 II 和厌氧途径的富集。未观察到 HPV 病毒载量与生态失调评分之间存在相关性。结论 多哥妇女的 HR-HPV 感染和宫颈发育不良与阴道微生物群失调有关,其特征是乳酸菌耗竭和厌氧、潜在促炎类群富集。这些发现表明微生物组对 HPV 阳性和宫颈病变有贡献,并支持将其纳入撒哈拉以南非洲的预防策略。这是第一项以西非社区为基础的研究,结合了盲法宫颈筛查、Nugent 评分和基于测序的微生物组分析。

title: Human Papilloma Virus detection through the cobas® 4800 system in women from Lima, Peru
abstract: Aim: Determine the prevalence of high-risk Human Papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection in women from Lima between 2012 and 2013 using the Cobas 4800 test.Method: The study included 5324 women aged 30 or over, whose cervical samples underwent the Cobas 4800 molecular test.Positive samples were analyzed through liquid-based cytology.Results: The prevalence of HR-HPV infection was 15.2%.Genotype 16 was found in 16.2%, genotype 18 in 3. 1% and genotypes 31, 33, 35, 39, 45, 51, 52, 56, 58, 59, 66, and 68 in 71.2%.62.8% of samples were identified without cytological changes, 19.8% with LSIL, 14% with ASCUS, 2% with HSIL, and 0.7% with ASC-H.Conclusion: The prevalence of HR-HPV in this study continues to be significant.In simple infections, the frequency of genotypes 16 and 18 stood out, and in coinfections, the group of the other twelve HPV-RA genotypes predominated.

title: Prevalence and Risk Factors Associated with Human Papilloma Virus Infection among Women Attending Selected Hospitals in Sokoto, Sokoto State, Nigeria
abstract: Human Papilloma Virus (HPV) infection is the primary cause of virtually all cervical cancers. Cervical cancer despite being largely preventable is still the leading cause of gynaecological cancer related death among females in developing countries. This study was carried out to determine the prevalence and risk factors associated with Human Papilloma Virus infection among women attending selected hospitals in Sokoto, Sokoto State, Nigeria. This study involves the use of questionnaire to obtain data on socio-demographic and risk factors as well as the analysis of high vaginal swab obtained from 208 women. The high vaginal swab samples were analysed for Human Papilloma Virus antigen using ELISA. Prevalence of 6.23% of Human papilloma virus infection was recorded in this study. Marital status, cigarette smoking, number of Co-wives, use of condom and age at first sex were identified as significant risk factors for Human papilloma virus infection in this study. This study identified a low burden of Human papilloma virus infection in Sokoto, Nigeria.
journal: JOURNAL OF BIOLOGY AND GENETIC RESEARCH

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to determine the prevalence and risk factors associated with Human Papilloma Virus (HPV) infection among women attending selected hospitals in Sokoto, Sokoto State, Nigeria. This was necessary because HPV infection is the primary cause of virtually all cervical cancers, and despite being largely preventable, cervical cancer remains the leading cause of gynaecological cancer-related death among females in developing countries.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted to assess HPV infection among 208 women attending selected hospitals in Sokoto, Sokoto State, Nigeria. The design involved the use of questionnaires to gather socio-demographic and risk factor data, as well as the analysis of high vaginal swab samples using ELISA.
analysis.methods: High vaginal swab samples were analyzed for HPV antigen using ELISA. The study did not report any additional laboratory or statistical procedures.
analysis.main_results: The study recorded a prevalence of 6.23% for HPV infection among the women. Marital status, cigarette smoking, number of co-wives, use of condoms, and age at first sex were identified as significant risk factors for HPV infection.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings, noting a low burden of HPV infection in Sokoto, Nigeria, and identified specific risk factors. The novelty of the study lies in its identification of these risk factors in the local population.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform surveillance and prevention strategies for HPV infection and associated cervical cancer in Sokoto, Nigeria. They highlight the importance of addressing identified risk factors to reduce the burden of HPV infection.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the use of a single diagnostic method (ELISA) and the small sample size, which may limit the generalizability of the findings. The evidence strength is moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study determined the prevalence and risk factors of HPV infection among women in Sokoto, Nigeria, finding a 6.23% prevalence and identifying specific risk factors. The findings can inform local surveillance and prevention strategies.

title: Recent therapeutic strategies for HPV-Associated head and neck cancers.
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated head and neck cancers (HNCs), particularly oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinomas (OPSCC), represent a growing global health burden with rapidly increasing incidence over recent decades. These tumours are biologically and clinically distinct from HPV-negative HNCs, occurring more frequently in younger individuals with limited exposure to traditional risk factors such as tobacco and alcohol. HPV-driven oncogenesis is mediated by viral oncoproteins E6 and E7, which disrupt genomic stability through inactivation of p53 and retinoblastoma pathways, promoting uncontrolled proliferation, genomic instability, and treatment resistance. Current therapeutic strategies for HPV-positive HNCs include surgery, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy, with cisplatin-based chemoradiotherapy remaining the standard of care for locoregionally advanced disease. However, improved treatment responses and overall prognosis in HPV-positive patients have stimulated interest in treatment de-escalation strategies aimed at reducing toxicity without compromising efficacy. Minimally invasive surgical approaches, such as transoral robotic surgery, and reduced-intensity radiotherapy regimens show promising functional outcomes. Immunotherapy represents a major advancement in recurrent and metastatic disease, with immune checkpoint inhibitors targeting the PD-1/PD-L1 axis demonstrating survival benefits in selected patient populations. Emerging approaches include therapeutic vaccines against HPV oncoproteins, adoptive T cell transfer, targeted therapies, oncolytic virotherapy, and gene therapy aimed at silencing E6/E7 expression or restoring tumor suppressor function. Nanomedicine further offers novel platforms for drug delivery, radiosensitization, and immunomodulation, enhancing treatment specificity and efficacy. Despite significant progress, major challenges persist, including limitations in early diagnosis, treatment resistance, biomarker-driven patient selection, and inadequate public awareness of HPV-associated cancer risk. Integration of advanced diagnostics, such as circulating tumor HPV DNA assays and next-generation sequencing, may improve risk stratification and treatment monitoring. Continued research into combination therapies, targeted approaches, and patient-tailored treatment algorithms remains essential to improve outcomes. In summary, evolving therapeutic strategies for HPV-associated HNCs reflect a shift toward precision oncology, focusing on improved survival, reduced toxicity, and personalized interventions driven by molecular tumor characteristics.

HPV-driven oncogenesis is mediated by viral oncoproteins E6 and E7, which disrupt genomic stability through inactivation of p53 and retinoblastoma pathways, promoting uncontrolled proliferation, genomic instability, and treatment resistance. Current therapeutic strategies for HPV-positive HNCs include surgery, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy, with cisplatin-based chemoradiotherapy remaining the standard of care for locoregionally advanced disease. However, improved treatment responses and overall prognosis in HPV-positive patients have stimulated interest in treatment de-escalation strategies aimed at reducing toxicity without compromising efficacy. Minimally invasive surgical approaches, such as transoral robotic surgery, and reduced-intensity radiotherapy regimens show promising functional outcomes. Immunotherapy represents a major advancement in recurrent and metastatic disease, with immune checkpoint inhibitors targeting the PD-1/PD-L1 axis demonstrating survival benefits in selected patient populations. Emerging approaches include therapeutic vaccines against HPV oncoproteins, adoptive T cell transfer, targeted therapies, oncolytic virotherapy, and gene therapy aimed at silencing E6/E7 expression or restoring tumor suppressor function. Nanomedicine further offers novel platforms for drug delivery, radiosensitization, and immunomodulation, enhancing treatment specificity and efficacy. Despite significant progress, major challenges persist, including limitations in early diagnosis, treatment resistance, biomarker-driven patient selection, and inadequate public awareness of HPV-associated cancer risk. Integration of advanced diagnostics, such as circulating tumor HPV DNA assays and next-generation sequencing, may improve risk stratification and treatment monitoring. Continued research into combination therapies, targeted approaches, and patient-tailored treatment algorithms remains essential to improve outcomes. In summary, evolving therapeutic strategies for HPV-associated HNCs reflect a shift toward precision oncology, focusing on improved survival, reduced toxicity, and personalized interventions driven by molecular tumor characteristics.
abstract_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 相关头颈癌 (HNC),特别是口咽鳞状细胞癌 (OPSCC),代表着日益严重的全球健康负担,近几十年来 发病率 迅速增加。这些肿瘤在生物学和临床上与 HPV 阴性 HNC 不同,更常见于接触烟草和酒精等传统危险因素有限的年轻个体。HPV 驱动的肿瘤发生是由病毒癌蛋白 E6 和 E7 介导的,它们通过 p53 和视网膜母细胞瘤途径的失活破坏基因组稳定性,促进不受控制的增殖、基因组不稳定和 治疗 耐药性。目前 HPV 阳性 HNC 的治疗策略包括手术、放疗和化疗,其中基于顺铂的放化疗仍然是局部晚期疾病的标准治疗方法。然而,HPV 阳性患者的 治疗 反应和总体预后的改善激发了人们对旨在降低毒性而不影响疗效的 治疗 降阶梯策略的兴趣。微创手术方法,例如经口机器人手术和降低强度放射治疗方案显示出有希望的功能结果。免疫疗法代表了复发性和转移性疾病的重大进步,针对 PD-1/PD-L1 轴的免疫检查点抑制剂在选定的患者群体中证明了生存获益。新兴方法包括针对 HPV 癌蛋白的治疗性 疫苗、过继性 T 细胞转移、靶向治疗、溶瘤病毒疗法以及旨在沉默 E6/E7 表达或恢复肿瘤抑制功能的基因治疗。纳米医学进一步提供了药物输送、放射增敏和免疫调节的新平台,增强了 治疗 的特异性和功效。尽管取得了重大进展,但重大挑战仍然存在,包括早期 诊断、治疗 耐药的局限性、生物标志物驱动的患者选择以及公众对 HPV 相关癌症风险的认识不足。先进诊断技术的整合,例如循环肿瘤 HPV DNA 检测和下一代测序,可以改善风险分层和 治疗 监测。对联合疗法、靶向方法和患者定制的 治疗 算法的持续研究对于改善结果仍然至关重要。总之,针对 HPV 相关 HNC 的不断发展的治疗策略反映了向精准肿瘤学的转变,重点是提高生存率、降低毒性以及由分子肿瘤特征驱动的个性化干预。

title: Current concern about HPV vaccine safety and self-reported HPV vaccination among female college students in mainland China: A weighted cross-sectional study
abstract: Concern about human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine safety is a potential correlate of vaccination among female college students in China. This weighted cross-sectional study used the 2025 National College Student Survey on Sexual and Reproductive Health, a voluntary, convenience-based online survey conducted across mainland China. The analytic sample comprised 37,329 vaccine-aware female junior-college and undergraduate students; 6,202 eligible respondents who did not know the HPV vaccine were examined separately in selection analyses. Vaccination was self-reported receipt of at least one HPV vaccine dose; dose number, series completion, vaccination date, and record verification were unavailable. Weighted Poisson generalized estimating equations clustered by school adjusted for age, school level, entry grade, region, monthly expenditure, pre-college residence, ethnicity, and maternal education. Vaccination was reported by 6,708/37,329 students (18.0% unweighted; 19.7% weighted). Compared with students who were not concerned, adjusted prevalence ratios were 0.60 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.54-0.67) for very concerned students, 0.55 (0.50-0.60) for concerned students, 0.70 (0.65-0.75) for neutral students, and 1.00 (0.86-1.16) for those not at all concerned. Standardized prevalence was 28.3% in the reference group and 15.5%-19.8% in the concerned and neutral groups. The categorical association departed from a single log-linear pattern ( P < .001) and remained stable across geographic, weighting, covariate, eligibility, and selection analyses. Current concern about HPV vaccine safety was associated with lower prior self-reported vaccination in this vaccine-aware student population. Communication and catch-up strategies warrant prospective evaluation with verified initiation and completion outcomes.

abstract_zh: 对 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 疫苗 安全性的担忧是中国女大学生中 疫苗接种 的潜在相关因素。这项加权横断面研究使用了 2025 年全国大学生性与生殖健康调查,这是一项在中国大陆进行的自愿、便利的在线调查。分析样本包括 37,329 名具有 疫苗 意识的女大专和本科生;在选择分析中,对 6,202 名不知道 HPV 疫苗 的合格受访者进行了单独检查。疫苗接种 自我报告接受至少一剂 HPV 疫苗 剂量;剂量编号、系列完成情况、疫苗接种 日期和记录验证不可用。按学校聚类的加权泊松广义估计方程,根据年龄、学校级别、入学年级、地区、每月支出、大学预科居住地、种族和母亲教育程度进行调整。6,708/37,329 名学生报告了 疫苗接种(18.0% 未加权;19.7% 加权)。与不关心的学生相比,非常关心的学生的调整后 患病率 比率为 0.60(95% 置信区间 [CI],0.54-0.67),关心的学生为 0.55(0.50-0.60),中性的学生为 0.70(0.65-0.75),完全不关心的学生为 1.00(0.86-1.16)。参考组的标准化 患病率 为 28.3%,相关组和中性组的标准化 患病率 为 15.5%-19.8%。分类关联偏离了单一对数线性模式 (P < .001),并且在地理、权重、协变量、资格和选择分析中保持稳定。当前对 HPV 疫苗 安全性的担忧与了解 疫苗 的学生群体中先前自我报告的 疫苗接种 较低有关。沟通和追赶策略需要通过验证的启动和完成结果进行前瞻性评估。

title: Hyperactivation of p53 and pRb is a potential therapeutic option in HPV driven cancers.
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is the most frequently acquired sexually transmitted infection. The E6 and E7 oncoproteins of HPV mainly contribute to the development of cancerous lesions by dysregulating the host p53 and pRb tumour suppressor pathways, respectively. Although prophylactic vaccines are available for HPV infection, they are ineffective for established HPV infections. Despite significant advances in surgery, radiotherapy, and systemic therapies, recurrent, metastatic, and treatment-resistant HPV-associated cancers continue to present substantial clinical challenges, highlighting the urgent need for novel therapeutic strategies.As the E6 and E7 viral oncoproteins are key drivers of HPV-positive cancer pathogenesis, targeting these proteins represents a rational approach for developing new therapies. Gene therapy is currently studied extensively as a potential strategy for cancer regression. RNA interference technology and CRISPR approaches are highly effective in downregulating the expression of viral oncoproteins. In most cancer types, tumour suppressor proteins are frequently mutated; however, in HPV-induced cancers, they typically remain wild type. Hence, increasing the bioavailability of tumour suppressor proteins is a therapeutic option. CRISPR activation (CRISPRa) is a CRISPR system variant in which catalytically inactive Cas9 (dcas9) is fused with a transcriptional activator to induce gene expression. Unlike CRISPR, CRISPRa increases the expression of the targeted gene without genomic modifications. Although there are few strategies available to increase the expression of tumour suppressor proteins, CRISPRa has gained a major focus as an effective and promising strategy. There is potential to develop CRISPRa as a future therapeutic intervention to treat HPV induced cancers combined with other treatment modalities.

title_zh: p53 和 pRb 的过度激活是 HPV 驱动的癌症的潜在治疗选择。
source_body_en: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is the most frequently acquired sexually transmitted infection. The E6 and E7 oncoproteins of HPV mainly contribute to the development of cancerous lesions by dysregulating the host p53 and pRb tumour suppressor pathways, respectively. Although prophylactic vaccines are available for HPV infection, they are ineffective for established HPV infections. Despite significant advances in surgery, radiotherapy, and systemic therapies, recurrent, metastatic, and treatment-resistant HPV-associated cancers continue to present substantial clinical challenges, highlighting the urgent need for novel therapeutic strategies.As the E6 and E7 viral oncoproteins are key drivers of HPV-positive cancer pathogenesis, targeting these proteins represents a rational approach for developing new therapies. Gene therapy is currently studied extensively as a potential strategy for cancer regression. RNA interference technology and CRISPR approaches are highly effective in downregulating the expression of viral oncoproteins. In most cancer types, tumour suppressor proteins are frequently mutated; however, in HPV-induced cancers, they typically remain wild type. Hence, increasing the bioavailability of tumour suppressor proteins is a therapeutic option. CRISPR activation (CRISPRa) is a CRISPR system variant in which catalytically inactive Cas9 (dcas9) is fused with a transcriptional activator to induce gene expression. Unlike CRISPR, CRISPRa increases the expression of the targeted gene without genomic modifications. Although there are few strategies available to increase the expression of tumour suppressor proteins, CRISPRa has gained a major focus as an effective and promising strategy. There is potential to develop CRISPRa as a future therapeutic intervention to treat HPV induced cancers combined with other treatment modalities.

title: Determinants of HPV self-sampling willingness for cervical cancer screening in Urban and Rural Areas of Thailand: An analytical cross-sectional study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV) self-sampling is a feasible strategy to increase cervical cancer screening coverage among under-screened populations. Still, the factors influencing willingness to use self-HPV testing in provincial Thai settings are limited. This study aimed to identify independent factors associated with willingness to use self-HPV testing among women in urban and rural areas of Thailand. METHODS: This analytical cross-sectional survey enrolled Thai women aged 25-60 years residing in Saraburi Province. This study used a structured self-administered questionnaire covering demographic characteristics, HPV knowledge, attitudes, and willingness to use self-HPV testing. Multivariable regression was used to estimate prevalence ratios (PRs). RESULTS: In total, 453 of 527 women (86.0%; 95% CI 82.8%-88.8%) were willing to use self-HPV testing. Knowledge score (PR 1.038 per 10% increase; 95% CI 1.016-1.061) and attitude score (PR 1.092 per 1-point increase; 95% CI 1.022-1.165) were significantly and independently associated with higher willingness, while low household income was significantly associated with lower willingness relative to middle income (PR 0.904; 95% CI 0.830-0.985). Residential area and screening history were not associated with willingness. CONCLUSIONS: Self-HPV willingness was high in both urban and rural settings among digitally accessible respondents, with no statistically significant difference between residential areas; this finding should not be extrapolated to women without digital access. Knowledge and attitudes were the strongest modifiable determinants identified, and this hypothetical willingness should be distinguished from actual uptake, which remains to be evaluated.

title: Love, Sex, and Immunosuppression: A Sexual Health Overview for the Transplant Clinician
abstract: Abstract Sexual health is a critical, yet often overlooked, aspect of comprehensive care for solid organ transplant recipients. While transplantation can restore overall health and quality of life, patients may continue to experience sexual dysfunction because of physiological, psychological, and pharmacological factors. Furthermore, transplant recipients remain at risk for sexually transmitted infections (STIs), including HIV, human papillomavirus (HPV), syphilis, and others, with implications for both patient and graft outcomes. HPV-associated malignancies, particularly anal squamous cell carcinoma, occur at significantly higher rates in this population, highlighting the need for recommendations on targeted screening and vaccination. This review addresses the spectrum of sexual health issues across transplant populations-including liver, kidney, heart, and lung recipients-with practical guidance on sexual function, STI screening, and risk reduction strategies. We outline current evidence and recommendations for preexposure and postexposure prophylaxis against HIV and bacterial STIs, including the use of tenofovir-based preexposure prophylaxis and doxycycline postexposure prophylaxis. We also aim to highlight the role of immunization against HPV, hepatitis B, hepatitis A, and monkeypox virus, emphasizing safety, timing, and efficacy considerations in immunocompromised individuals. Despite growing awareness, implementation of routine sexual health assessment and STI prevention strategies remains inconsistent in transplant medicine. We call for greater integration of sexual health into transplant care pathways and identify key research priorities to optimize outcomes. Clinicians should feel empowered to initiate open conversations, advocate for vaccination and prophylaxis, and tailor care based on individualized risk. This comprehensive update offers practical tools and recommendations to improve sexual health in solid organ transplant recipients.

abstract_zh: 摘要 性健康是实体器官移植受者综合护理的一个重要但经常被忽视的方面。虽然移植可以恢复整体健康和生活质量,但由于生理、心理和药理因素,患者可能会继续出现性功能障碍。此外,移植受者仍然面临性传播感染 (STI) 的风险,包括 HIV、人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV)、梅毒等,这对患者和移植结果都有影响。HPV 相关恶性肿瘤,特别是肛门鳞状细胞癌,在该人群中的发生率明显较高,这凸显了针对针对性筛查和 疫苗接种 提出建议的必要性。这篇综述讨论了移植人群(包括肝脏、肾脏、心脏和肺脏受者)的一系列性健康问题,并提供了性功能、性传播感染筛查和降低风险策略的实用指导。我们概述了针对艾滋病毒和细菌性传播感染的暴露前和暴露后预防的当前证据和建议,包括使用基于替诺福韦的暴露前预防和多西环素暴露后预防。我们还旨在强调针对 HPV、乙型肝炎、甲型肝炎和猴痘病毒的免疫接种的作用,强调对免疫功能低下个体的安全性、时机和有效性考虑。尽管人们的认识不断提高,但移植医学中常规性健康评估和性传播感染预防策略的实施仍然不一致。我们呼吁将性健康更多地纳入移植护理途径,并确定关键研究重点以优化结果。临床医生应该感到有权发起公开对话,倡导 疫苗接种 和预防,并根据个体化风险定制护理。这一全面的更新提供了实用的工具和建议,以改善实体器官移植受者的性健康。

title: Reducing the burden of cervical cancer in Zambia in the next 40 years: impact of enhanced screening efforts
abstract: BACKGROUND: Zambia bears one of the world's highest cervical cancer burdens, driven by high human papillomavirus (HPV) prevalence, gaps in vaccination and screening, and the intersecting human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) epidemic. METHODS: In this study we assess the potential impact of scaling up HPV screening alongside vaccination efforts, based on a community outreach plan designed by ICAP Columbia and Zambia's Ministry of Health. The plan targets Zambia's rural communities and promotes self-collection of samples, on-site HPV testing, and same-day treatment when eligible, with referral to hub sites for severe cases. To estimate the expanded screening's impact, we developed an individual-based model capturing HPV transmission through age-structured sexual partnership, and subsequent progression from infection to cervical lesions and cervical cancer. The model was calibrated to Zambia's demographic profile, 2022 HPV prevalence, 2020 cervical cancer incidence. We compared five 40-year scenarios: no intervention, vaccination only (girls 9-14 years); vaccination plus visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA)-based screening targeted towards women living with HIV, and scenarios extending screening to all women ( ~ 200,000 vs ~400,000 tests/year with 5% annual increase). Outcomes were cervical cancer incidence, percent reduction across intervention scenarios, and cumulative cases averted. Uncertainty was quantified via repeated stochastic simulations with bootstrap confidence intervals (CIs). Sensitivity analyses examined alternative HIV incidence trajectories and reduced screening accessibility. RESULTS: By 2060, HPV vaccination alone reduces cervical cancer incidence by 47% (95% CI: 39%-55%) compared to current rates but has limited effect in the first 20 years. Adding population screening accelerates impact: under ~400,000 tests/year, incidence falls 64% (95% CI: 56%-70%) by year 20 and 97% (95% CI: 96%-98%) by year 40, averting ~35,000 cases by 2040 and ~183,000 by 2060 and reaching the World Health Organization elimination threshold by 2060. Exploratory analyses suggest additional long-term benefit from vaccinating boys, especially when vaccination coverage is suboptimal. CONCLUSIONS: In Zambia, vaccination alone will not meaningfully reduce cervical cancer burden in the near term, and pairing vaccination with a community-based HPV-screening/treatment could prevent tens of thousands of cancer cases within two decades and place elimination within reach.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了赞比亚因高 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 患病率、疫苗接种 和筛查方面的差距以及艾滋病毒流行而造成的高负担。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究利用 ICAP Columbia 和赞比亚卫生部设计的社区外展计划,评估了在赞比亚农村社区扩大 HPV 筛查以及 疫苗接种 工作的潜在影响。
elements_zh.methods: 开发了一个基于个体的模型来估计 HPV 筛查和 疫苗接种 的影响,并根据赞比亚的人口概况和 2022 HPV 患病率 进行校准,结果包括 宫颈癌 发病率 和通过随机模拟和敏感性分析避免的病例。
elements_zh.main_results: 到 2060 年,与目前的比率相比,仅 HPV 疫苗接种 就可将 发病率 降低 47%(95% CI:39%-55%),但增加人群筛查会加速影响,到 20 年将 发病率 降低 64%(95% CI:56%-70%),到 20 年降低 97%(95% CI:95% CI: 96%-98%)到40年,在二十年内避免了数以万计的病例。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究表明,将 疫苗接种 与基于社区的 HPV 筛查相结合,可以在二十年内预防数以万计的癌症病例,并使赞比亚的消除目标触手可及。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可为减少赞比亚 宫颈癌 负担的策略提供信息,特别是通过将 HPV 筛查与农村社区的 疫苗接种 工作相结合。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性包括对结果模型的依赖、需要进一步探索替代的 HIV 发病率 轨迹以及降低筛查可及性,对结果的可信度中等。

abstract_zh: 背景:由于 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 患病率 高、疫苗接种 和筛查方面的差距以及人类免疫缺陷病毒 (HIV) 的交叉流行,赞比亚是世界上 宫颈癌 负担最重的国家之一。方法:在这项研究中,我们根据 ICAP 哥伦比亚和赞比亚卫生部设计的社区外展计划,评估了与 疫苗接种 努力一起扩大 HPV 筛查的潜在影响。该计划针对赞比亚的农村社区,提倡自我采集样本、现场 HPV 检测以及符合条件的当天 治疗,并将严重病例转介至中心地点。为了估计扩大筛查的影响,我们开发了一个基于个体的模型,通过年龄结构的性伴侣以及随后从感染到宫颈病变和 宫颈癌 的进展来捕获 HPV 传播。该模型根据赞比亚的人口特征、2022 HPV 患病率、2020 宫颈癌 发病率 进行了校准。我们比较了 5 种 40 年情景:无干预,仅 疫苗接种(9-14 岁女孩);疫苗接种 加上基于醋酸 (VIA) 筛查的目视检查,针对感染艾滋病毒的女性,以及将筛查范围扩大到所有女性的方案(每年约 200,000 次测试与约 400,000 次测试,每年增加 5%)。结果为 宫颈癌 发病率、干预方案的减少百分比以及避免的累积病例。通过使用引导置信区间 (CI) 进行重复随机模拟来量化不确定性。敏感性分析检查了替代的 HIV 发病率 轨迹并降低了筛查的可及性。结果:到 2060 年,与目前的比率相比,单独使用 HPV 疫苗接种 可使 宫颈癌 发病率 降低 47%(95% CI:39%-55%),但在前 20 年效果有限。增加人群筛查可加速影响:每年约 400,000 次检测,发病率 到 20 年下降 64%(95% CI:56%-70%),到 40 年下降 97%(95% CI:96%-98%),到 2040 年避免约 35,000 例病例,到 2060 年避免约 183,000 例病例,并达到世界卫生组织的目标到 2060 年消除阈值。探索性分析表明,为男孩接种疫苗具有额外的长期益处,特别是当 疫苗接种 覆盖率不理想时。结论:在赞比亚,短期内单独使用 疫苗接种 并不能显着减少 宫颈癌 负担,而将 疫苗接种 与基于社区的 HPV 筛查/治疗 结合起来可以在二十年内预防数以万计的癌症病例,并使消除指日可待。

analysis_zh.main_results: 到 2060 年,与目前的比率相比,仅 HPV 疫苗接种 就可将 发病率 降低 47%(95% CI:39%-55%),但增加人群筛查会加速影响,到 20 年将 发病率 降低 64%(95% CI:56%-70%),到 20 年降低 97%(95% CI:95% CI: 96%-98%)到40年,在二十年内避免了数以万计的病例。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究表明,将 疫苗接种 与基于社区的 HPV 筛查相结合,可以在二十年内预防数以万计的癌症病例,并使赞比亚的消除目标触手可及。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可为减少赞比亚 宫颈癌 负担的策略提供信息,特别是通过将 HPV 筛查与农村社区的 疫苗接种 工作相结合。

title: Pre-implementation assessment of upstream domains on the uptake of HPV self-sampling in safety-net settings: a scoping review.
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) screening can be used as an early detector for cervical cancer. The newly US Food and Drug Administration-approved HPV self-sampling tests can be used by safety net practices in the USA to help mitigate the current screening disparities seen in patients. As patient acceptability and capability have already been established, this scoping review synthesizes the barriers and facilitators of implementing HPV self-sampling from the perspective of safety net providers and leadership, and the upstream factors not yet explored in current research. Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, a literature search was conducted exploring peer-reviewed publications and grey literature to establish the current landscape of HPV self-sampling. Findings were organized using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research. From the 57 works included, it was found that safety net practices are capable of implementing HPV self-sampling by utilizing current workflows and team members. However, outer setting guidelines and policies heavily influence the implementation process, likely causing a delay in uptake by safety net practices. Recent guideline endorsements and forthcoming insurance coverage address several of these barriers, making post-approval implementation research in safety net settings an urgent priority.

title: Health Economic Impact and Cost Threshold for Switching From Bivalent to Nonavalent HPV Vaccination for Preadolescent Girls in KwaZulu Natal, South Africa: A Mathematical Modeling Analysis Accounting for the HIV Epidemic.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus bivalent (2vHPV) and nonavalent (9vHPV) vaccines protect against HPV types causing 70% and 90% of cervical cancers, respectively. South African guidelines recommend vaccinating girls ages 9-14 with 1 dose of 2vHPV. Switching recommendations to 9vHPV could avert more cervical cancer burden, but the cost-effectiveness and cost-threshold of 9vHPV in South Africa is unknown. METHODS: Using a validated compartmental HPV and HIV transmission model parameterized to KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, we simulated scenarios of 2vHPV and 9vHPV implementation over 100 years with 2 doses (72% coverage) and 1 dose (80% and 90% coverage) with lifelong or waning single-dose vaccine efficacy. We evaluated cervical cancer cases and deaths averted. We also estimated the maximum cost/dose for 9vHPV to be cost-effective using willingness-to-pay thresholds from $500/disability-adjusted life-year (DALY) averted to $3015/DALY averted (2023 USD). We also assessed the incremental cost-effectiveness ratios of 9vHPV at current costs ($110/dose) compared with 2vHPV ($9.23/dose). RESULTS: Single-dose 9vHPV at 80% coverage could avert 7.9% more cervical cancer cases and 6.4% more deaths than 2vHPV (lifelong efficacy). The maximum 9vHPV price to be cost-effective (lifelong efficacy, 80% coverage) ranged from $15 ($500/DALY averted threshold) to $45/dose ($3015/DALY averted threshold). At current market costs, single-dose 9vHPV at 90% coverage exceeds commonly used cost-effective thresholds with incremental cost-effectiveness ratios of $10,480/DALY averted (lifelong efficacy) and $8806/DALY averted (waning efficacy). CONCLUSIONS: Implementing 9vHPV can result in a greater reduction in cervical cancer burden than 2vHPV, but vaccine costs need to be reduced for 9vHPV to be cost-effective in KwaZulu-Natal.
journal: Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999)

title: Determining the Challenges and Opportunities for Increasing HPV Vaccine Awareness in Bangladesh: A Qualitative Study
abstract: ABSTRACT Background and Aims Cervical cancer remains a major public health issue in low‐ and middle‐income countries, including Bangladesh, where awareness of cervical cancer and the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine is limited. To reduce the disease burden, Bangladesh launched a free HPV vaccination program for girls ages 10–14 in 2023. However, coverage remains low due to limited reach, low awareness, and cultural resistance. This study examined the challenges and opportunities that influence HPV vaccine awareness and uptake in Bangladesh. Methods A total of 25 Key Informant Interviews (KIIs) and In‐Depth Interviews (IDIs) were completed, comprising 9 KIIs and 16 IDIs, including an Expanded Program on Immunization (EPI) program manager (n = 2); a Civil Surgeon (n = 1); community health workers (n = 3); religious leaders (n = 3); parents (n = 4); teachers (n = 6); and students (n = 6) from Dhaka, Chittagong, and Cox's Bazar districts. All interviews were transcribed verbatim and analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis (Braun & Clarke) to identify key themes related to barriers and facilitators of vaccine awareness and acceptance. Results We identified four major themes and 12 sub‐themes. Findings revealed a significant lack of understanding among adolescent girls about cervical cancer symptoms, prevention, and the importance of HPV vaccination. Negative perceptions among community health workers, parents, and teachers, particularly in rural areas, further hindered vaccine uptake. Religious and cultural concerns were major barriers to acceptance. Participants suggested that organizing teacher–parent meetings, school‐based health education sessions, and awareness campaigns could help increase vaccine acceptance and understanding. Conclusions Knowledge and perceptions about HPV vaccination varied across stakeholder groups, influencing overall vaccine acceptance. Tailored, community‐based educational interventions are crucial to address misconceptions and enhance awareness among adolescents and key community influencers. Strengthening multi‐sectoral collaboration could increase HPV vaccination coverage and support cervical cancer prevention efforts in Bangladesh.

abstract_zh: 摘要 背景和目标 宫颈癌 仍然是低收入和中等收入国家的一个主要公共卫生问题,其中包括孟加拉国,这些国家对 宫颈癌 和 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 疫苗 的认识有限。为了减轻疾病负担,孟加拉国于 2023 年针对 10-14 岁女孩启动了免费 HPV 疫苗接种 计划。然而,由于覆盖范围有限、意识低下和文化阻力,覆盖率仍然较低。本研究探讨了影响孟加拉国 HPV 疫苗 认知和使用的挑战和机遇。方法 完成了总共 25 名关键知情人访谈 (KII) 和深度访谈 (IDI),其中 9 名 KII 和 16 名 IDI,其中包括一名扩大免疫规划 (EPI) 项目经理 (n = 2);一名民间外科医生(n = 1);社区卫生工作者(n = 3);宗教领袖(n = 3);父母(n = 4);教师(n = 6);以及来自达卡、吉大港和考克斯巴扎尔地区的学生 (n = 6)。所有访谈均逐字记录,并使用反思性主题分析(Braun & Clarke)进行分析,以确定与 疫苗 认知和接受的障碍和促进因素相关的关键主题。结果 我们确定了 4 个主要主题和 12 个子主题。调查结果显示,青春期女孩对 宫颈癌 症状、预防以及 HPV 疫苗接种 的重要性严重缺乏了解。社区卫生工作者、家长和教师(尤其是农村地区)的负面看法进一步阻碍了 疫苗 的采用。宗教和文化问题是接受的主要障碍。参与者建议,组织教师家长会、校本健康教育课程和宣传活动有助于提高 疫苗 的接受度和理解。结论 不同利益相关群体对 HPV 疫苗接种 的了解和看法各不相同,影响了 疫苗 的整体接受度。量身定制的、基于社区的教育干预措施对于消除误解并提高青少年和主要社区影响者的认识至关重要。加强多部门合作可以提高 HPV 疫苗接种 覆盖率并支持孟加拉国的 宫颈癌 预防工作。

title: Clinical testing source is associated with observed HPV burden in hospital-based cervical HPV genotyping: a retrospective study of 36,362 women
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hospital-based cervical HPV genotyping datasets include women tested through different clinical pathways, so observed HPV burden may vary by source population. We quantified source-specific HPV burden and evaluated cytology-linked context. METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective observational study of 36,362 women with one retained index HPV test per woman. All underwent uniform 23-type cervical HPV genotyping by PCR-reverse dot blot and were classified as health examination attendees or gynecology outpatients by clinical testing source. Primary outcomes were any HPV positivity, 12-type carcinogenic HPV positivity, and multiple-genotype infection. Source-group prevalence ratios were adjusted for age group and calendar quarter of testing. Cytology was linked within a prespecified ±3-day window. RESULTS: The cohort included 9,969 health examination attendees and 26,393 gynecology outpatients; cytology was linked for 34,049 women (93.6%). Compared with health examination attendees, gynecology outpatients had higher any HPV positivity (28.7% vs 17.2%; adjusted PR, 1.61; 95% CI, 1.54-1.69), 12-type carcinogenic HPV positivity (19.4% vs 10.7%; adjusted PR, 1.75; 95% CI, 1.65-1.86), and multiple-genotype infection (9.2% vs 3.9%; adjusted PR, 2.23; 95% CI, 2.01-2.48). HPV16/18 and HPV52/58 positivity also varied across cytology strata. Source-group contrasts were attenuated but remained in the same direction after exclusion of an HPV/STI-related clinical-label subset and after restriction to women with linked cytology. CONCLUSIONS: Clinical testing source was associated with substantial differences in observed HPV burden within a uniform hospital laboratory workflow, highlighting the importance of clinical setting and source population when hospital-based HPV estimates are interpreted.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the association between clinical testing source and observed HPV burden in a hospital-based cervical HPV genotyping dataset of 36,362 women. However, the study's retrospective design and potential for residual confounding limit the strength of the evidence, which is assessed as moderate.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 基于医院的宫颈 HPV 基因分型数据集包括通过不同临床途径进行测试的女性,因此观察到的 HPV 负担可能因来源人群而异。我们量化了特定来源的 HPV 负荷并评估了细胞学相关的背景。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们对 36,362 名女性进行了一项单中心回顾性观察研究,每名女性进行了一次保留指数 HPV 检测。所有患者均接受统一的PCR-反向斑点杂交23型宫颈HPV基因分型,并按临床检测来源分类为体检参加者或妇科门诊患者。
elements_zh.methods: 主要结果是任何 HPV 阳性、12 型致癌 HPV 阳性和多基因型感染。源组 患病率 比率根据年龄组和测试日历季度进行调整。细胞学在预先指定的±3天窗口内进行关联。
elements_zh.main_results: The cohort included 9,969 health examination attendees and 26,393 gynecology outpatients; cytology was linked for 34,049 women (93.6%). Compared with health examination attendees, gynecology outpatients had higher any HPV positivity (28.7% vs 17.2%; adjusted PR, 1.61; 95% CI, 1.54-1.69), 12-type carcinogenic HPV positivity (19.4% vs 10.7%; adjusted PR, 1.75; 95% CI, 1.65-1.86), and multiple-genotype infection (9.2% vs 3.9%; adjusted PR, 2.23; 95% CI, 2.01-2.48).
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 临床检测来源与统一医院实验室工作流程中观察到的 HPV 负担存在显着差异相关,这凸显了在解释基于医院的 HPV 估计值时临床环境和来源人群的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果告诫不要在不考虑临床环境和来源人群的情况下解释基于医院的 HPV 估计值,这可能会影响观察到的 HPV 负担并为更准确的 监测 和 诊断 策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 在排除 HPV/STI 相关临床标签子集以及限制具有相关细胞学的女性后,来源组对比有所减弱,但仍保持相同方向。由于回顾性设计和潜在的残留混杂因素,证据是中等的。

analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果告诫不要在不考虑临床环境和来源人群的情况下解释基于医院的 HPV 估计值,这可能会影响观察到的 HPV 负担并为更准确的 监测 和 诊断 策略提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 在排除 HPV/STI 相关临床标签子集以及限制具有相关细胞学的女性后,来源组对比有所减弱,但仍保持相同方向。由于回顾性设计和潜在的残留混杂因素,证据是中等的。

title: Natural killer cell dysfunction in cervical cancer: HPV-driven immune evasion through the tumor immune microenvironment barrier
abstract: Cervical cancer, driven by persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV), remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Natural killer (NK) cells are critical mediators of antitumor immunity, and their dysfunction in cervical cancer has been reported. However, current understanding remains uneven, with most studies focusing on isolated mechanisms rather than providing an integrated view of how the HPV-mediated tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) impairs NK cell functions in cervical cancer. In this review, we integrate HPV-driven immune modulation with TIME remodeling to examine how structural, cellular, molecular, and metabolic constraints may converge to restrict NK cell infiltration and function in cervical cancer, distinguishing cervical cancer-specific, HPV-associated, and cross-tumor evidence. Furthermore, we discuss emerging therapeutic strategies targeting these barriers and emphasize their potential as complementary approaches to existing immunotherapies, while noting that most remain preclinical or hypothesis-generating in cervical cancer. This framework provides a unified perspective to guide the development of more effective NK cell–based immunotherapies in cervical cancer.
journal: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 由高危 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 持续感染驱动的 宫颈癌 仍然是全球癌症相关 死亡率 的主要原因。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 然而,目前的理解仍然不平衡,大多数研究侧重于孤立的机制,而不是提供关于 HPV 介导的肿瘤免疫微环境 (TIME) 如何损害 宫颈癌 中 NK 细胞功能的综合观点。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 在这篇综述中,我们将 HPV 驱动的免疫调节与 TIME 重塑相结合,以研究结构、细胞、分子和代谢约束如何聚合以限制 宫颈癌 中的 NK 细胞浸润和功能,区分 宫颈癌 特异性、HPV 相关和跨肿瘤证据。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 此外,我们讨论了针对这些障碍的新兴治疗策略,并强调它们作为现有免疫疗法的补充方法的潜力,同时指出,宫颈癌 中的大多数策略仍处于临床前或假设生成阶段。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该框架提供了一个统一的视角来指导 宫颈癌 中更有效的基于 NK 细胞的免疫疗法的开发。

title: Uptake of the HPV vaccine in girls and boys with an intellectual disability: a systematic review.
abstract: Abstract Background Cervical cancer is the fourth most common female cancer and is preventable by (human papillomavirus) HPV vaccination, given to adolescent girls and boys in most World Health Organisation countries. People with an intellectual disability have significantly worse cancer outcomes than the general population, attributable to deficits in prevention, screening, early diagnosis and treatment, and there is concern that rates of HPV vaccination may be lower in this population. The aim was to undertake a systematic review of research into HPV vaccination uptake in people with intellectual disability, and influences on vaccination. Methods Multiple databases (Medline; Embase; CINAHL; PsycINFO; Cochrane Central; Overton) were searched to May 2026. Quantitative, qualitative and mixed-methods studies were eligible if they: (i) reported rates of HPV vaccination uptake in people with an intellectual disability, or (ii) reported factors influencing HPV vaccination in people with an intellectual disability. Two reviewers independently screened studies and took inclusion decisions. Data extraction and quality appraisal (JBI tools) were undertaken by one researcher and verified by another. Data on vaccination initiation and completion rates were synthesised narratively and meta-analysed (risk ratio, RR) as appropriate; influences on vaccination were mapped to the Socio-Ecological Model. Results 25 studies (18 quantitative; 7 qualitative) from eight high-income countries were included. Meta-analyses showed that girls and boys with intellectual disability were less likely to receive the vaccine (RR 0.74 and 0.56, respectively) and complete a vaccine course (RR 0.63 and 0.55, respectively), compared to those without intellectual disability. Reported barriers were primarily individual but also occurred at interpersonal, institutional or societal levels. The quantitative and qualitative studies were generally of high quality. Conclusions Girls and boys with an intellectual disability are less likely than those without intellectual disability to receive HPV vaccines, or complete a vaccine course once started, increasing cancer risk. Identified barriers and facilitators indicate opportunities in the healthcare and education sectors to intervene to reduce this inequity. Future research is needed from a wider range of countries, including data from people with intellectual disability themselves. Registration The protocol was registered with the OSF in September 2025: https://osf.io/7h8cz/overview

The aim was to undertake a systematic review of research into HPV vaccination uptake in people with intellectual disability, and influences on vaccination. abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 宫颈癌 是第四种最常见的女性癌症,可通过 (人乳头瘤病毒) HPV 疫苗接种 进行预防,在大多数世界卫生组织国家,该病毒可用于青春期女孩和男孩。由于预防、筛查、早期 诊断 和 治疗 方面的缺陷,智力障碍人士的癌症结果明显比一般人群差,并且有人担心该人群中 HPV 疫苗接种 的感染率可能较低。目的是对智力障碍人群中 HPV 疫苗接种 的摄取及其对 疫苗接种 的影响进行系统回顾。方法 检索多个数据库(Medline;Embase;CINAHL;PsycINFO;Cochrane Central;Overton)至 2026 年 5 月。定量、定性和混合方法研究符合条件,如果:(i) 报告智力障碍人群中 HPV 疫苗接种 的摄取率,或 (ii) 报告影响智力障碍人群中 HPV 疫苗接种 的因素。两名评审员独立筛选研究并做出纳入决定。数据提取和质量评估(JBI 工具)由一名研究人员进行,并由另一名研究人员进行验证。酌情对 疫苗接种 启动率和完成率的数据进行叙述性综合和荟萃分析(风险比,RR);对 疫苗接种 的影响被映射到社会生态模型。结果 纳入来自八个高收入国家的 25 项研究(18 项定量;7 项定性)。荟萃分析显示,与无智力障碍的女孩和男孩相比,有智力障碍的女孩和男孩接受 疫苗(分别为 RR 0.74 和 0.56)并完成 疫苗 课程(分别为 RR 0.63 和 0.55)的可能性较小。报告的障碍主要是个人的,但也发生在人际、机构或社会层面。定量和定性研究总体上是高质量的。结论 与无智力障碍的女孩和男孩相比,患有智力障碍的女孩和男孩接受 HPV 疫苗 或一旦开始就完成 疫苗 课程的可能性较小,从而增加了癌症风险。已确定的障碍和促进因素表明医疗保健和教育部门有机会进行干预,以减少这种不平等。未来的研究需要来自更广泛的国家,包括来自智力障碍者本身的数据。注册 该协议于 2025 年 9 月在 OSF 注册:https://osf.io/7h8cz/overview

title: Post‐Transplant Vaccine Coverage Among Pediatric Solid Organ Transplant Recipients in Canada: A Canadian Immunization Research Network Study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Children with solid organ transplants are at increased risk for vaccine-preventable infections, yet data on vaccine coverage remain limited. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study to evaluate post-transplant vaccine coverage at three tertiary pediatric hospitals in Canada. Vaccine coverage was summarized descriptively; subgroup comparisons and multivariable logistic regression were performed. RESULTS: Among 272 subjects (median age at transplant 3 years; mean follow-up 7.27 years), "overall vaccine coverage," defined as receipt of all recommended non-live, non-seasonal vaccines, was 39.7% (95% CI 34.1-45.6). When stratified by transplant organ subgroup, overall vaccine coverage was significantly lower among heart/lung transplant recipients (24.0%) compared to kidney (51.7%; p < 0.001) and liver/multivisceral transplant recipients (40.9%; p = 0.018). Coverage for individual vaccines ranged from 83.8% to 96.3% for those administered according to standard schedules but was lower for vaccines requiring additional doses for SOT recipients, including higher-valency pneumococcal (71.9%) and human papillomavirus vaccines (56.7%). No demographic or clinical factors were associated with overall vaccine coverage; however, urban residence was associated with higher human papillomavirus vaccine uptake. CONCLUSION: Our findings underscore the need for improved strategies to optimize immunization coverage in pediatric solid organ transplant recipients in what is, to our knowledge, the largest and only multicenter study of its kind to date.

title: Molecular subtyping, prognostic model construction, and immune microenvironment analysis of cervical squamous cell carcinoma based on metabolic health and disease prevention
abstract: Background: Cervical squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC) development is modulated not only by HPV infection but also by host metabolic health. Purpose and method: This study characterised disulfidptosis-related genes (DRGs) in 241 TCGA-CESC and 300 GSE44001 patients to build a prognostic model and interpret it within a metabolic health-oriented prevention framework. Seventeen differentially expressed DRGs, enriched in glycolysis, fatty acid metabolism, and redox homeostasis, defined three metabolic-distinct molecular subtypes. Result: A six-gene DRG-score (DSTN, TLN1, MTHFD1L, MYH10, TXN, SLC7A11) and nomogram predicted prognosis effectively (C-index 0.747/0.665; 1-year AUC 0.835). High-risk tumours showed an immunosuppressed phenotype (immunotherapy response 20.0% vs. 71.9%) concordant with obesity- and diabetes-associated immune dysfunction, and reduced sensitivity to methotrexate, implicating one-carbon metabolism. Conclusion: These findings indicate that metabolic health optimisation—weight control, nutrition, physical activity, and management of diabetes and dyslipidemia—constitutes a modifiable pillar of CSCC prevention complementary to HPV vaccination and screening, warranting prospective validation with DRG-based stratification.

title: Association of JAM3/PAX1 methylation with cervical lesion severity and CIN2+ detection in hrHPV-positive women: a hospital-based study
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between JAM3/PAX1 methylation and cervical lesion severity and assess its diagnostic performance, alone and in combination with HPV16/18 genotyping, for detecting cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or higher (CIN2+) in hrHPV-positive women. METHODS: A total of 205 treatment-negative hrHPV-positive women with available JAM3/PAX1 methylation results and histopathological diagnoses were included in this hospital-based study. The association between methylation positivity and cervical lesion severity was evaluated using the Cochran-Armitage trend test. A subset of 105 participants with complete HPV genotyping, cytology, methylation, and histopathological data was further analyzed using ordinal logistic regression and diagnostic performance measures, including sensitivity, specificity, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). RESULTS: Among the 205 participants, JAM3/PAX1 methylation positivity increased with cervical lesion severity, with positivity rates of 20.00% in the normal group, 23.53% in CIN1, 33.33% in CIN2, 61.43% in CIN3, and 65.12% in cervical cancer (P for trend < 0.001). In the complete-data subset (n = 105), JAM3/PAX1 methylation positivity (OR = 5.02, 95% CI: 2.15-11.77) and HPV16/18 positivity (OR = 3.88, 95% CI: 1.75-8.60) were independently associated with higher cervical lesion grades. Parallel testing of JAM3/PAX1 methylation and HPV16/18 genotyping achieved a sensitivity of 86.81% and a specificity of 50.00% for CIN2+ detection, whereas sequential testing yielded a sensitivity of 43.96% and a specificity of 92.86%. CONCLUSION: JAM3/PAX1 methylation positivity was associated with cervical lesion severity in hrHPV-positive women. Combining JAM3/PAX1 methylation with HPV16/18 genotyping provided different sensitivity-specificity trade-offs for CIN2+ detection. These findings suggest that JAM3/PAX1 methylation may serve as an adjunctive marker for cervical lesion risk assessment, although further validation in larger and less-selected screening populations is needed.

source_records.abstract: Objective To evaluate the association between JAM3/PAX1 methylation and cervical lesion severity and assess its diagnostic performance, alone and in combination with HPV16/18 genotyping, for detecting cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or higher (CIN2+) in hrHPV-positive women. title: Synchronous Primary Cervical Adenocarcinoma and Colonic Adenocarcinoma: A Case Report and Literature Review.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Synchronous primary cervical and colorectal malignancies are uncommon and may be mistaken for metastatic disease, particularly when both tumors are adenocarcinomas. This article describes the diagnostic process and multidisciplinary treatment approach for a case of synchronous human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated uterine cervical adenocarcinoma (UAC) and colorectal adenocarcinoma (CRC). CASE PRESENTATION: A 47-year-old woman presented with postmenopausal bleeding. Cervical biopsy showed adenocarcinoma, and preoperative computed tomography unexpectedly demonstrated thickening at the descending-sigmoid junction; colonoscopy confirmed a second adenocarcinoma. The cervical tumor was diffusely positive for p16, CK7, and PAX8, and negative for CK20, CDX2, and SATB2, whereas the colon tumor showed robust positive expression for CK20, CDX2, and SATB2 and absence of CK7 and PAX8 expression. The morphology, immunophenotype, and somatic profiles support that these two tumors are distinct primary tumors. Following multidisciplinary teamwork (MDT), simultaneous laparoscopic radical hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, pelvic lymphadenectomy, and extended left hemicolectomy were performed. The patient was discharged on postoperative Day 5 without complications. Final pathology revealed the UAC at FIGO 2018 Stage IB1 (AJCC 9th edition pT1b1N0M0) and CRC at AJCC 9th edition pT3N2aM0. The patient received eight cycles of the CapeOX regimen postoperatively for node-positive CRC. At the 12-month follow-up, the patient remained disease-free. CONCLUSION: Synchronous pelvic adenocarcinomas should not be deemed metastatic disease. Combined anatomical, morphological, immunophenotypic, and molecular findings supported independent cervical and colonic primaries in this patient. MDT enabled simultaneous minimally invasive surgery and tumor-specific adjuvant therapy. More case data and longer term follow-up are required to substantiate the characteristics and outcomes of multiple primary synchronous cancers (MPSCs).

title: β‐Sitosterol Inhibits Cervical Carcinogenesis by Modulating the HMGB1/Wnt3a/β‐catenin Signaling Pathway
abstract: Cervical cancer (CC) continues to pose a major threat to women's health worldwide, a situation exacerbated by the suboptimal efficacy of existing treatment strategies. This study aimed to explore the inhibitory effect of β-sitosterol (SIT) on cervical cancer progression and elucidate its underlying molecular mechanism. The anti-tumor effects of SIT were evaluated through in vitro assays (CCK-8, colony formation, flow cytometry, wound healing, Transwell) and an in vivo xenograft mouse model. Mechanistic studies, including Western blotting, molecular docking, and immunohistochemistry (IHC) were assessed. Subsequently, HMGB1-knockdown cell lines were established to examine the role of HMGB1 in tumor formation and to assess its associated signaling pathways in vitro. The results showed that in vitro, SIT treatment significantly inhibited the proliferation and colony formation of cervical cancer cells, while inducing G2-phase arrest. These effects were accompanied by the downregulation of HMGB1, HPV16/18-E6, Wnt3a, and β-catenin. HMGB1 was confirmed to be overexpressed in cervical cancer, and its knockdown attenuated malignant phenotypes and reduced the expression of pathway-related proteins. Consistently, both SIT treatment and HMGB1 knockdown suppressed tumor growth in vivo without inducing obvious toxicity. In conclusion, SIT inhibits cervical cancer progression, potentially through modulating the HMGB1/Wnt3a/β-catenin signaling pathway; however, further mechanistic validation is required. Nonetheless, these findings provide a rationale for repurposing SIT as a candidate against cervical cancer.

The anti-tumor effects of SIT were evaluated through in vitro assays (CCK-8, colony formation, flow cytometry, wound healing, Transwell) and an in vivo xenograft mouse model. Mechanistic studies, including Western blotting, molecular docking, and immunohistochemistry (IHC) were assessed. Subsequently, HMGB1-knockdown cell lines were established to examine the role of HMGB1 in tumor formation and to assess its associated signaling pathways in vitro. The results showed that in vitro, SIT treatment significantly inhibited the proliferation and colony formation of cervical cancer cells, while inducing G2-phase arrest. These effects were accompanied by the downregulation of HMGB1, HPV16/18-E6, Wnt3a, and β-catenin. HMGB1 was confirmed to be overexpressed in cervical cancer, and its knockdown attenuated malignant phenotypes and reduced the expression of pathway-related proteins. Consistently, both SIT treatment and HMGB1 knockdown suppressed tumor growth in vivo without inducing obvious toxicity. In conclusion, SIT inhibits cervical cancer progression, potentially through modulating the HMGB1/Wnt3a/β-catenin signaling pathway; however, further mechanistic validation is required. Nonetheless, these findings provide a rationale for repurposing SIT as a candidate against cervical cancer.

title: State-level variation in HPV vaccination initiation among U.S. adolescents after accounting for individual and provider factors
abstract: BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination prevents HPV-related cancers, yet coverage among U.S. adolescents has plateaued. This study examined whether state-level variation in HPV vaccination initiation persisted after accounting for provider recommendation and individual characteristics. METHODS: We analyzed 2024 National Immunization Survey-Teen data from 14,622 adolescents aged 13-17 years (mean age = 15.04, SD = 1.40). Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression examined provider-verified HPV vaccination initiation (≥1 dose), adjusting for parent-reported healthcare provider recommendation, age, sex, race and ethnicity, poverty status, maternal education, health insurance, and state of residence. Adjusted state-level predicted probabilities were estimated using predictive margins. RESULTS: State of residence remained jointly associated with HPV vaccination initiation after adjustment (design-adjusted Wald test: F[50, 14,502] = 3.76, p < 0.001). Parent-reported healthcare provider recommendation was strongly associated with initiation (AOR = 3.12, 95% CI: 2.67-3.65). Older adolescents had higher odds of HPV vaccination initiation (AOR = 1.17, 95% CI: 1.12-1.23), whereas no significant difference was observed between female and male adolescents. Compared with Hispanic adolescents, non-Hispanic White adolescents had lower odds of initiation (AOR = 0.63, 95% CI: 0.51-0.78). Maternal education and health insurance were also jointly associated with initiation. Adjusted predicted probabilities ranged from 64.5% in Mississippi to 89.7% in Hawaii, a 25.2-percentage-point difference. CONCLUSIONS: State-level variation in HPV vaccination initiation persisted after accounting for parent-reported healthcare provider recommendation and measured sociodemographic and healthcare-related characteristics. These findings support further investigation of place-related contextual factors that may contribute to state-level variation in HPV vaccination coverage.

title: EVALUATION OF SCREENING PROTOCOLS IN GYNECOLOGIC ONCOLOGY IN PUBLIC HEALTH CARE
abstract: Cervical cancer represents a significant public health problem, associated mainly with persistent infection by oncogenic human papillomavirus (HPV). Continuous screening is an essential preventive strategy for the early detection of precursor lesions. However, significant challenges persist in Brazil arising from low cytopathological coverage, regional disparities and discontinuity in the care provided. This study aimed to analyze the scientific evidence on cervical cancer screening methods and the obstacles to their effective implementation in the Brazilian Unified Health System (SUS). This is a narrative literature review conducted in the PubMed database using the descriptors "Early Detection of Cancer" and "Genital Neoplasms, Female". The findings show an excess of tests performed outside the recommended age range, marked socioeconomic barriers and limited access to confirmatory diagnosis and treatment. Molecular HPV DNA tests have high potential to improve primary screening, although their incorporation requires a substantial expansion of care capacity and of the support network. It is concluded that the effectiveness of early detection depends on the consolidation of an organized screening model, on tackling inequities in access and on guaranteeing a comprehensive line of care for women.
journal: International Journal of Health Management Review

The findings show an excess of tests performed outside the recommended age range, marked socioeconomic barriers and limited access to confirmatory diagnosis and treatment. Molecular HPV DNA tests have high potential to improve primary screening, although their incorporation requires a substantial expansion of care capacity and of the support network. It is concluded that the effectiveness of early detection depends on the consolidation of an organized screening model, on tackling inequities in access and on guaranteeing a comprehensive line of care for women.

title: Radiotherapy 2.0: The art of doing less to treat head and neck tumors more effectively
abstract: The management of squamous cell carcinomas of the head and neck is undergoing a major conceptual shift. Long guided by a logic of therapeutic escalation - where the goal was to maximize tumor control at the cost of significant functional sequelae - the field is increasingly moving toward precision personalization. This paradigm shift, which can be described as "Radiotherapy 2.0", is partly driven by the emergence of human papillomavirus-positive oropharyngeal tumors, whose favorable prognosis, particularly in younger and more active patients, has prompted renewed consideration of the balance between the probability of cure and long-term quality of life. The goal is therefore not only to cure, but also to "cure better". This approach - doing less to treat better - is supported by a growing body of clinical evidence suggesting that treatment intensity may be safely reduced in appropriately selected patients. From a geometric standpoint, the emphasis is on anatomical sparing: whether it involves preserving the pharyngeal constrictor muscles to reduce late dysphagia, or omitting prophylactic contralateral cervical irradiation in well-localized cases, selective reduction of irradiation volumes is increasingly being investigated. Quantitatively, reducing physical doses may be feasible when targeting intermediate-risk histological profiles in the adjuvant setting or when relying on dynamic biological selection. In this regard, early tumor response to induction chemotherapy or the assessment of hypoxia via molecular imaging (fluoromisonidazole positron-emission tomography) may represent useful selection tools, including for approaches involving substantial dose reduction to 30 Gy. At the same time, radiobiological optimization of treatment duration through moderate hypofractionation represents a potential therapeutic alternative, reducing treatment duration while maintaining acceptable toxicity. However, this quest for dose de-escalation has also encountered important limitations and requires careful patient selection. Recent data suggest that empirically weakening key components of treatment - whether by replacing cisplatin with cetuximab or by substantially reducing the dose in the presence of lymph node capsule rupture - may increase the risk of locoregional failure. Radiotherapy 2.0 should therefore not be based on empirical treatment reduction, but rather on carefully defined clinical, anatomical and, where available, biological criteria to determine the appropriate dose and treatment volume for each patient.

abstract_zh: 头颈部鳞状细胞癌的治疗正在经历重大的概念转变。长期以来,在治疗升级逻辑的指导下——目标是以重大功能性后遗症为代价最大限度地控制肿瘤——该领域正日益朝着精准个性化方向发展。这种范式转变可以被描述为“放射治疗2.0”,部分原因是人乳头瘤病毒阳性口咽肿瘤的出现,其良好的预后,特别是在年轻和活跃的患者中,促使人们重新考虑治愈概率和长期生活质量之间的平衡。因此,我们的目标不仅是治愈,而且是“更好地治愈”。这种方法——减少治疗效果,得到越来越多的临床证据的支持,表明在适当选择的患者中可以安全地降低 治疗 强度。从几何角度来看,重点是解剖学上的保留:无论是保留咽缩肌以减少晚期吞咽困难,还是在局部病例中省略预防性对侧颈部照射,选择性减少照射量的研究越来越多。从数量上讲,当在佐剂环境中针对中等风险组织学特征或依赖动态生物选择时,减少物理剂量可能是可行的。在这方面,早期肿瘤对诱导化疗的反应或通过分子成像(氟米索硝唑正电子发射断层扫描)评估缺氧可能代表有用的选择工具,包括涉及将剂量大幅减少至 30 Gy 的方法。同时,通过适度大分割对 治疗 持续时间进行放射生物学优化是一种潜在的治疗替代方案,可减少 治疗 持续时间,同时保持可接受的毒性。然而,这种剂量递减的探索也遇到了重要的限制,需要仔细选择患者。最近的数据表明,根据经验削弱 治疗 的关键成分 - 无论是用西妥昔单抗替代顺铂,还是在淋巴结包膜破裂的情况下大幅减少剂量 - 可能会增加局部失败的风险。因此,放射治疗 2.0 不应基于经验性的 治疗 减少,而应基于仔细定义的临床、解剖学和(如果有)生物学标准,以确定每位患者的适当剂量和 治疗 体积。
