title: Cost-utility analysis of HPV-cytology co-testing in the Korean national cervical cancer screening program
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the cost-utility of incorporating human papillomavirus (HPV) testing into the Korean National Cervical Cancer Screening Program, across 30 strategies. METHODS: A Markov model of cervical cancer compared no screening, cytology screening, and HPV-cytology co-testing among women aged ≥20 years from the healthcare system perspective over a lifetime horizon. Natural-history parameters were calibrated to age-specific incidence in the Korea Central Cancer Registry. Costs and quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) were discounted at 4.5%, and a willingness-to-pay (WTP) threshold of 30 million Korean won (KRW) per QALY applied. RESULTS: Compared with no screening, biennial cytology had an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) of 1.8 million KRW/QALY, 6% of the WTP threshold. Only 4 of the 26 co-testing strategies remained on the efficiency frontier, and none was cost-effective: ICERs versus biennial cytology ranged from 100.5 million KRW/QALY for the most efficient strategy (biennial co-testing at ages 35-70 years with biennial cytology at other ages) to 118.4 million KRW/QALY for biennial co-testing at all ages, 3.4-3.9 times the threshold. Findings were unchanged at 0% and 3% discount rates and in one-way sensitivity analyses; biennial cytology was optimal in 99.6% of probabilistic simulations. Even the most efficient co-testing strategy would become cost-effective only if the HPV test price fell below 19,007 KRW. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that biennial cytology remains economically efficient under current Korean conditions and that the addition of HPV testing would not be cost-effective at the present WTP threshold. Reconsideration may be warranted if HPV testing costs decrease substantially.

title: Public Health Action against Cancer across Awareness, Primary Prevention and Early Detection: Evidence, Equity and Implementation
abstract: Background: Cancer remains a leading cause of death worldwide, and its burden is shifting towards countries with the least capacity to diagnose and treat it. Public health action, including the promotion of awareness, primary prevention and early detection, is widely presented as the most efficient response, yet the evidence supporting each component differs substantially in type, strength and transferability. Objectives: This critical narrative review examines what public health interventions in cancer awareness, primary prevention, screening and early diagnosis of symptomatic disease have been shown to achieve, where the evidence is contested, and how equity and implementation conditions shape population benefit. Methods: Literature published between January 2000 and September 2026 was identified through structured searches of biomedical and multidisciplinary scholarly databases, authoritative institutional repositories and citation tracking. Randomised trials, quasi-experimental policy evaluations, cohort and registry studies, modelling studies, systematic reviews and consensus statements were appraised qualitatively for design appropriateness, outcome relevance, risk of bias and transferability, and synthesised thematically. Results: The strongest population-level evidence supports fiscal and regulatory tobacco control, vaccination against human papillomavirus and hepatitis B virus, and organised cervical and colorectal screening. Evidence for alcohol pricing and labelling is persuasive but rests mainly on non-cancer or intermediate outcomes. Symptom-awareness campaigns change knowledge and referral activity, but their effects on stage at diagnosis are small and their effects on mortality remain undemonstrated. Breast, lung and prostate screening produce disease-specific mortality benefits that depend heavily on risk targeting, programme quality and the handling of overdiagnosis, while effects on all-cause mortality are rarely detectable. Multi-cancer blood tests and artificial intelligence have advanced faster than evidence of patient benefit. Across the continuum, socioeconomic gradients in exposure, participation and stage at diagnosis recur, and coverage in many low- and middle-income settings remains far below that required for population impact. Conclusions: Public health cancer control is most defensible when it prioritises structural prevention and organised, quality-assured early detection, judges new technologies against mortality and harm outcomes, and treats equitable reach as a primary outcome rather than an afterthought.

title: Hybrids of 4-cyano-2-aryl-1,3-oxazole-5-sulfonamides with a 3-phenyl-1,2,4-oxadiazole motif: rational design, synthesis, in silico profiling, and antiproliferative activity against HepG2, A549, T98G, and HeLa human cancer cell lines
abstract: Multi-target anticancer agents attract growing interest for overcoming resistance and improving selectivity. Hybrids combining 1,2,4-oxadiazole and 1,3-oxazole scaffolds may target multiple oncogenic pathways simultaneously, yet the structural determinants of their activity remain poorly defined. Fourteen 1,3-oxazole/1,2,4-oxadiazole hybrids were designed, synthesized, and tested against HeLa, A549, HepG2, and T98G cancer lines, with non-cancerous NCTC clone 929 for selectivity. Two series were prepared: acyclic-linked hybrids (2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12; –(CH2)n–, n = 2-7) and piperidine-linked analogs (13, 14). Activity depended steeply on linker length, peaking in compound 12 (n = 7), the most potent derivative (HeLa CC50 = 14.73 ± 2.02 μM; A549 CC50 = 43.92 ± 3.71 μM; HepG2 CC50 = 394.95 ± 24.01 μM; SI = 8 toward HeLa). Compounds 13 and 14 were inactive. Analysis of molecular geometry and electronic structure across the –(CH2)n–, series suggests compounds 2, 4, and 6 cannot engage productively with protein active sites: their tweezer-like geometry directs electron density into intramolecular contacts rather than outward-facing interactions. Lengthening the linker in 8, 10, and 12 shifts the geometry toward a more linear arrangement. Docking predicts interaction with the E6AP-binding pocket of HPV18 E6, with compound 12 occupying it at ΔG = –9.0 kcal/mol, consistent with the pronounced sensitivity of HPV18-positive HeLa cells. Virtual profiling implicated stress-response signaling (ARE, MMP, ATAD5) and aromatase. Compound 12 showed very low similarity to ChEMBL bioactives (p ≤ 0.3) and low predicted target-interaction probability, suggesting a potentially unrecognized mechanism. Linker length thus emerges as the principal determinant of antiproliferative activity in this hybrid class, defining compound 12 as a lead for HPV-associated cancers, with activity hypothesized to disrupt the oncogenic E6-E6AP interaction.

title: Comparative Transcriptomic Profiling of Endometriosis and Ovarian Clear Cell Carcinoma: An Exploratory RNA-Sequencing Case Series
abstract: Background: Endometriosis is associated with an increased risk of ovarian clear cell carcinoma (OCCC), but the molecular differences between these conditions remain incompletely understood. We investigated transcriptomic differences among benign endometriosis, endometriosis-associated OCCC, and OCCC without an identified endometriotic background. Methods: RNA sequencing was performed on ovarian tissues from 13 patients: five with benign endometriosis, three with endometriosis-associated OCCC, and five with OCCC without an identified endometriotic background. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified using DESeq2, followed by pathway enrichment analysis using Enrichr and KEGG. Results: We identified 646 DEGs overlapping between comparisons of benign endometriosis and each OCCC group. EEF1A2, TLX3, TMEM252, and LEFTY1 showed increased expression in both OCCC groups. Gene sets annotated to seven KEGG pathways were significantly enriched: cytoskeleton in muscle cells, complement and coagulation cascades, extracellular matrix–receptor interaction, human papillomavirus infection, integrin signaling, Hippo signaling, and p53 signaling. Conclusions: This exploratory RNA-sequencing study identified differences in gene expression between benign ovarian endometriosis and the OCCC groups in this cohort, along with significant enrichment of gene sets associated with several biological pathways. Given the small sample size, differences in age between groups, confounding by sequencing batch, absence of a normal ovarian tissue comparator, and lack of independent validation, these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger, independent cohorts.

Results: We identified 646 DEGs overlapping between comparisons of benign endometriosis and each OCCC group. EEF1A2, TLX3, TMEM252, and LEFTY1 showed increased expression in both OCCC groups. Gene sets annotated to seven KEGG pathways were significantly enriched: cytoskeleton in muscle cells, complement and coagulation cascades, extracellular matrix–receptor interaction, human papillomavirus infection, integrin signaling, Hippo signaling, and p53 signaling. Conclusions: This exploratory RNA-sequencing study identified differences in gene expression between benign ovarian endometriosis and the OCCC groups in this cohort, along with significant enrichment of gene sets associated with several biological pathways. Given the small sample size, differences in age between groups, confounding by sequencing batch, absence of a normal ovarian tissue comparator, and lack of independent validation, these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger, independent cohorts.

title: Engineering programmable isothermal amplification and CRISPR/Cas12a for nucleic acid detection
abstract: Rapid and multiplex nucleic acid detection remains limited by assay complexity and nonspecific signals. This thesis investigated simplified, programmable strategies based on isothermal amplification and CRISPR/Cas12a. Different assay formats examined CRISPR-triggered amplification, in situ crRNA generation and promoter-independent self-transcription using human papillomavirus (HPV) and miR-21 as model targets. An abstract model-based hairpin amplification system was first evaluated for HPV16 detection. Putative self-folding products were observed, but poor reproducibility and persistent non-specific amplification prevented reliable detection. A separate CRISPR/Cas12a-integrated loop amplification strategy was developed, in which two core primers initiated target recognition and staggered cleavage-based amplification. The strategy detected HPV16, HPV18 and HPV52 and produced amplification responses from mixed HPV16/18 samples and individually tested HPV targets under triplex primer conditions in both two-step and one-pot formats. The two-step triplex assay produced distinguishable melting peaks for the individually tested targets, while reliable genotype discrimination in mixed samples was not established. In another strategy, extended recombinase polymerase amplification primers were designed so that the amplicons generated crRNA through transcription. Primer-derived transcription was identified as a major source of background and suppressed by reducing primer concentration. The three-step assay detected 10 copies of HPV16 per reaction, while the two-in-one format detected 100 copies and showed good specificity. An unexpected primer-derived signal was subsequently repurposed to establish Self-Transcribing Self-Recognition CRISPR (STSR-CRISPR). Designed ssDNA templates generated RNA-containing products through promoter-independent transcription and supported Cas12a activation without a conventional promoter or externally synthesised crRNA. However, mechanistic complexity and variation between independent transcription reactions prevented reliable analytical characterisation. Together, these studies show how assigning additional functions to reaction components can simplify different assay formats and support multiplex detection. They also identify unintended pathways as a central design challenge for lower-complexity CRISPR-based detection.

title: Bidirectional Integration of Family Planning, Cervical Cancer Screening, and HIV Services in Sub-Saharan Africa: A Scoping Review of Delivery Models and Implementation Outcomes (2020–2026)
abstract: REVIEW QUESTION: What service-delivery models, clinical uptake outcomes, and implementation determinants characterize the bidirectional integration of family planning, cervical cancer screening, and HIV care across healthcare facilities in Sub-Saharan Africa between 2020 and 2026? METHODOLOGY: This scoping review follows the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology and will be reported according to PRISMA-ScR guidelines. ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA (PCC): - Population: Women of reproductive age (15–49 years) living with or at risk of HIV, and healthcare providers/facilities in Sub-Saharan Africa. - Concept: Bidirectional service integration models linking HIV testing, antiretroviral therapy (ART), or viral load care with family planning (contraceptive counseling/provision) and/or cervical cancer screening (VIA, HPV DNA testing, cytology, thermal ablation/cryotherapy). - Context: Primary, secondary, or tertiary healthcare facilities in Sub-Saharan Africa, published between January 1, 2020 and December 31, 2026 in English or French. - Exclusions: Narrative reviews, editorials, commentaries, study protocols without empirical data, studies outside Sub-Saharan Africa, and standalone vertical clinics without cross-service linkage. SEARCH STRATEGY: Systematic searches will be conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, WHO Global Index Medicus, and African Journals Online (AJOL) for studies published between 2020 and 2026. Core PubMed Search String: ("HIV Infections"[MeSH] OR "HIV"[Title/Abstract] OR "antiretroviral therapy"[Title/Abstract] OR "ART clinic*"[Title/Abstract]) AND ("Family Planning Services"[MeSH] OR "Contraception"[MeSH] OR "family planning"[Title/Abstract] OR "contracept*"[Title/Abstract] OR "Uterine Cervical Neoplasms"[MeSH] OR "cervical cancer screening"[Title/Abstract] OR "visual inspection with acetic acid"[Title/Abstract] OR "HPV testing"[Title/Abstract]) AND ("Delivery of Health Care, Integrated"[MeSH] OR "integrat*"[Title/Abstract] OR "one-stop"[Title/Abstract] OR "co-locat*"[Title/Abstract] OR "bidirectional"[Title/Abstract] OR "link*"[Title/Abstract]) AND ("Africa South of the Sahara"[MeSH] OR "Sub-Saharan Africa"[Title/Abstract] OR "Nigeria"[Title/Abstract] OR "Kenya"[Title/Abstract] OR "Uganda"[Title/Abstract] OR "South Africa"[Title/Abstract] OR "Tanzania"[Title/Abstract] OR "Zambia"[Title/Abstract] OR "Malawi"[Title/Abstract] OR "Zimbabwe"[Title/Abstract] OR "Ethiopia"[Title/Abstract] OR "Ghana"[Title/Abstract] OR "Rwanda"[Title/Abstract] OR "Mozambique"[Title/Abstract] OR "Botswana"[Title/Abstract]) SCREENING & DATA EXTRACTION: Citations will be deduplicated and screened blindly by two independent reviewers in Rayyan (Title/Abstract followed by Full-Text review). Data on country, facility tier, integration model (one-stop, co-located, or facilitated referral), contraceptive/cervical screening uptake, HIV care outcomes, and health-system barriers/enablers will be charted in a standardized matrix and synthesized descriptively.

title: Molecular detection of viral pathogens associated with loose shell syndrome in cultured mangrove crabs (Scylla spp.)
abstract: Mangrove crabs (Scylla spp.) represent a high-value commodity in the Philippine aquaculture industry. However, emerging disease conditions, including loose shell syndrome (LSS), increasingly threaten the sustainability of their production and have contributed to significant declines. LSS in mangrove crabs is clinically characterized by a soft, loose carapace; reduced body mass associated with muscular atrophy; erratic behavior; and elevated mortality rates. The etiology of LSS remains unclear and may involve a combination of infectious agents and sub-optimal environmental conditions. To investigate the potential link between viral pathogens and LSS, this study screened mangrove crabs exhibiting clinical signs of the disease for selected viruses using polymerase chain reaction (PCR). A total of fifty-four (54) mangrove crabs showing symptoms of LSS were collected from aquaculture ponds in Capiz Province, Philippines. Genomic DNA was extracted from gut tissues and subjected to PCR assays targeting four viral pathogens: Hepatopancreatic Parvovirus (HPV), Infectious Hypodermal and Hematopoietic Necrosis Virus (IHHNV), Monodon Baculovirus (MBV), and White Spot Syndrome Virus (WSSV), following established diagnostic protocols. PCR screening detected all four viral pathogens, with IHHNV showing the highest prevalence at 14.8% of samples analyzed. Although the overall prevalence of each virus was relatively low, detecting these viral pathogens in LSS-affected crabs suggests a possible association with the syndrome. Further investigations, including pathogenicity studies and co-infection analyses, are warranted to clarify the role of these viral agents in LSS development and progression and to inform evidence-based health management strategies for the mangrove crab aquaculture industry.

title: Investigating the morphomolecular complexity of oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma
abstract: Background HPV drives a growing share of oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinomas (OPSCCs) in the UK and Ireland. Although HPV-positive disease usually carries a favourable prognosis, outcomes vary, and current testing relies on binary p16 immunohistochemistry with molecular confirmation. Aims To refine risk stratification in HPV-positive OPSCC using epidemiological, digital pathology, transcriptomic and health economic approaches. Methods A systematic review characterised HPV genotypes in UK and Irish non-cervical cancers. In population-representative OPSCC cohorts, HPV biomarkers were digitally quantified and related to survival, with external validation. Bulk and spatial transcriptomics explored tumour biology. Health economic modelling compared HPV testing strategies. Results The review defined the HPV genotype landscape in non-cervical cancers. Quantitative biomarker expression showed prognostic trends within HPV-positive disease. Transcriptomic analysis identified candidate prognostic markers linked to the tumour microenvironment. Alternative testing strategies offered potential cost savings without compromising health outcomes. Conclusions HPV-positive OPSCC is biologically heterogeneous in ways binary classification misses. Quantitative viral and microenvironmental biomarkers warrant prospective validation to support more precise, cost-conscious treatment stratification.

title: KAJIAN HUBUNGAN ANTARA STATUS EKONOMI, INFORMASI TENAGA KESEHATAN, DAN KESADARAN DETEKSI DINI KANKER SERVIKS
abstract: Pemeriksaan IVA (Inspeksi Visual Asam Asetat) digunakan untuk deteksi dini Human Papilloma Virus (HPV) pada leher rahim. Masalah yang dihadapi adalah rendahnya partisipasi wanita usia subur dalam pemeriksaan IVA. Data survei menunjukkan bahwa pada bulan Maret, sebanyak 145 (97%) wanita usia subur tidak melakukan pemeriksaan IVA. Tujuan penelitian ini adalah untuk menginvestigasi hubungan antara status ekonomi dan paparan informasi oleh tenaga kesehatan tentang deteksi dini kanker serviks dengan keikutsertaan pemeriksaan IVA di Wilayah Kerja Puskesmas Campurejo. Konsep-konsep utama dalam penelitian ini adalah status ekonomi, paparan informasi, dan pemeriksaan IVA. Metode penelitian yang digunakan adalah inferensial, lapangan, cross-sectional, survei, eks post facto, analitik korelasional, dan primer. Populasi penelitian ini adalah wanita usia subur yang memenuhi kriteria inklusi. Sampel terdiri dari 56 responden yang dipilih menggunakan teknik purposive sampling. Analisis data dilakukan dengan menggunakan korelasi Spearman. Hasil analisis menunjukkan bahwa sebagian besar responden memiliki status ekonomi rendah (50,0%), tidak mendapatkan paparan informasi dari tenaga kesehatan (60,7%), dan tidak mengikuti pemeriksaan IVA (71,4%). Upaya yang dilakukan termasuk penyuluhan kesehatan komprehensif dan meningkatkan kesadaran keluarga tentang pentingnya pemeriksaan IVA secara dini

Masalah yang dihadapi adalah rendahnya partisipasi wanita usia subur dalam pemeriksaan IVA. Data survei menunjukkan bahwa pada bulan Maret, sebanyak 145 (97%) wanita usia subur tidak melakukan pemeriksaan IVA. Tujuan penelitian ini adalah untuk menginvestigasi hubungan antara status ekonomi dan paparan informasi oleh tenaga kesehatan tentang deteksi dini kanker serviks dengan keikutsertaan pemeriksaan IVA di Wilayah Kerja Puskesmas Campurejo. Konsep-konsep utama dalam penelitian ini adalah status ekonomi, paparan informasi, dan pemeriksaan IVA. Metode penelitian yang digunakan adalah inferensial, lapangan, cross-sectional, survei, eks post facto, analitik korelasional, dan primer. Populasi penelitian ini adalah wanita usia subur yang memenuhi kriteria inklusi. Sampel terdiri dari 56 responden yang dipilih menggunakan teknik purposive sampling. Analisis data dilakukan dengan menggunakan korelasi Spearman. Hasil analisis menunjukkan bahwa sebagian besar responden memiliki status ekonomi rendah (50,0%), tidak mendapatkan paparan informasi dari tenaga kesehatan (60,7%), dan tidak mengikuti pemeriksaan IVA (71,4%). Upaya yang dilakukan termasuk penyuluhan kesehatan komprehensif dan meningkatkan kesadaran keluarga tentang pentingnya pemeriksaan IVA secara dini

title: Heme oxygenase and indoleamine regulation by cytokines in cervical cancer cells and natural killer cells cytotoxic activity
abstract: Objective: To determine the effect of the cytokines interleukin (IL-4), IL-10, Interferon gamma (IFN-γ) and tumor necrosis factor (TNF-α) in protein expression of HO-1 and IDO in cervical cancer cell lines and the cytotoxicity of NK cells in co-culture with cervix cancer cells pretreated with HO-1 and IDO inhibitors.Methods: The cervical cancer cell lines HeLa (HPV 18+), SiHa (HPV 16+) and C-33A (HPV -) were treated with 20 ng/mL of IL-4, IL-10, IFN-γ and TNF-α for 3 h, 6 h and 12 h, after that protein expression was assessed by flow cytometry.The cytotoxic activity of NK cells was performed in real time for 4 h.Results: Protein expression of the enzymes were changed at early times, increasing the expression of the enzymes in the 3 cell lines.We observed an increase in cytotoxic activity of NK cells cocultured with HeLa cells pretreated with the HO-1 inhibitor and in SiHa cells pretreated with the IDO inhibitor.Conclusion: The suppressor enzyme IDO is positively regulated by IL-10 in HeLa, SiHa, and NK cytotoxic activity increase in Hela and SiHa cells pretreated with HO-1 and IDO inhibitors respectively, which could be part of tumor escape mechanisms in cervix cancer.

title: Association between viral infections and male infertility. Prospects for the use of recombinant interferon alfa-2b (Viferon®) in the treatment of HPV/herpesvirus-associated male infertility
abstract: Связи между вирусными инфекциями и мужским бесплодием уделяется большое внимание уже много лет. В статье представлен обзор литературы, в котором представлены результаты исследований, подтверждающие неблагоприятное воздействие вирусных инфекций на параметры эякулята и эффективность программ вспомогательных репродуктивных технологий, рассмотрены патогенетические механизмы, с помощью которых ВПЧ и герпес-вирусы вызывают репродуктивные нарушения у мужчин, а также показана эффективность применения рекомбинантного интерферона альфа-2b с комплексом антиоксидантов, витаминами Е и С, при мужском бесплодии, ассоциированном с ВПЧ и герпес-вирусами.

full_text: ObjectiveTo examine the association between baseline erythrocyte folate and reversal, persistence, and progression of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 1 (CIN1).MethodsThis community-based prospective cohort included 564 Chinese women with CIN1, with follow-up assessments at 6, 12, and 24 months. Baseline erythrocyte folate was measured by chemiluminescence immunoassay. Histological outcomes were classified as reversal, persistence, or progression to CIN2 or worse (CIN2+); persistence and progression formed a composite adverse outcome. Analyses included Cox regression, restricted cubic splines, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. Exploratory experiments assessed proliferation and apoptosis in C33A and CaSki cervical cancer cells.ResultsAmong the 453 women assessed at 24 months, 342 (75.5%) had reversal, 58 (12.8%) had persistence, and 53 (11.7%) had progression to CIN2+. Lower baseline erythrocyte folate was associated with the composite adverse outcome in the reported adjusted model (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] = 2.42, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.62–3.61). No statistically significant nonlinearity was detected for this outcome at 6 or 12 months (p = 0.655 and p = 0.127), whereas an L-shaped association was observed at 24 months (P for nonlinearity = 0.005). At 24 months, the area under the ROC curve (AUC) for folate was 0.703 (95% CI: 0.647–0.760) overall and 0.742 (95% CI: 0.646–0.837) within the high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV)-positive subgroup. Higher nominal folate concentrations reduced proliferation and increased apoptosis in the two cell lines.ConclusionLower baseline erythrocyte folate was associated with adverse CIN1 outcomes after adjustment for the covariates included in the reported model. Event-time assumptions and residual confounding limit interpretation. These findings do not establish causality, an interaction with HR-HPV, or a therapeutic benefit of folate supplementation. Prognostic use requires further validation. 2Materials and methods2.1Study participantsParticipants were recruited from a community cohort established in two counties of Shanxi Province, China, using predefined eligibility criteria described previously (17). Of 39,971 women screened using the ThinPrep cytologic test (TCT), 37,219 had negative cytology and 2,752 had atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance or worse (ASC-US+). After excluding women with incomplete information (n = 387) or who declined follow-up (n = 68), 2,297 underwent HPV testing, colposcopy, and histological examination. Ten inadequate samples were excluded, leaving 2,287 women: 1,503 with a normal cervix (NC), 564 with CIN1, 218 with CIN2/3, and 2 with squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). The present analysis included the 564 women with CIN1 (Figure 1). The study was approved by the Ethics Committee of Shanxi Medical University (no. 2013-003), and all participants provided written informed consent.Figure 1Participant flow. Of 39,971 women screened, 37,219 had negative cytology and 2,752 had ASC-US+. After exclusion of 387 women with incomplete information and 68 who declined follow-up, 2,297 underwent further examination. Ten inadequate specimens were excluded, leaving 2,287 women with the diagnostic categories shown; the 564 women with CIN1 entered the present study. TCT, ThinPrep cytologic test; NILM, negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy; ASC-US+, atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance or worse; HPV, human papillomavirus; NC, normal cervix; CIN1, cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 1; CIN2/3, cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grades 2 or 3; SCC, squamous cell carcinoma.Flowchart showing participant selection for a study starting with 39,971 at baseline, divided into NILM (37,219) and ASC-UC+ (2,752). Exclusions and follow-up processes result in enrollment of subgroups NC (1,503), CIN1 (564), CIN2/3 (218), and SCC (2) into the present study.2.2Data and sample collectionTrained investigators conducted face-to-face interviews using a standardized questionnaire to collect demographic characteristics, lifestyle factors, personal hygiene practices, menstrual and sexual history, and family history of tumors. A 2 mL venous blood sample was collected in an anticoagulant tube for erythrocyte folate measurement. Exfoliated cervical cells were collected for HPV typing. Samples were stored at −80 °C. HPV genotyping and erythrocyte folate measurement were performed within 2 and 5 days, respectively.2.3Definition of exposure and outcomeWomen with CIN1 at baseline were scheduled for histological follow-up at 6, 12, and 24 months. Baseline erythrocyte folate concentration defined the exposure. At each visit, histology was compared with baseline: NC was classified as reversal, CIN1 as persistence, and CIN2 + as progression. Persistence and progression were combined as a composite adverse outcome for selected analyses, while their separate frequencies and associations were also reported because they differ in clinical significance. CIN2 + denotes CIN2 or worse and should not be interpreted as invasive cancer alone. Women diagnosed with CIN2 + received treatment according to clinical guidelines (18). Visit-specific outcome proportions were calculated among women assessed at the corresponding visit.2.4Detection of erythrocyte folateErythrocyte folate was measured by chemiluminescence immunoassay using a folate assay kit (Beckman Coulter, United States) according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Hematocrit was measured, and blood samples were hemolyzed before folate measurement against a calibration curve. The reported calculation was: erythrocyte folate (ng/mL) = [folate concentration in the hemolysate (ng/mL) × dilution factor] / [hematocrit (%) / 100].2.5HPV detection and typingExfoliated cervical cells were processed for HPV DNA extraction and flow-through hybridization using a kit from Chaozhou Kaipu Biochemical Company, China. The assay identified 15 high-risk and 6 low-risk HPV types, as described previously (17). Detection of any high-risk type was classified as HR-HPV positive; absence of the assayed high-risk types was classified as HR-HPV negative.2.6Exploratory cell culture and folate exposureHPV-negative C33A and HPV-positive CaSki cervical cancer cell lines (Academy of Medical Sciences, China) were cultured in MEM-EBSS and RPMI-1640 medium, respectively, supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum and penicillin–streptomycin. Cells were maintained at 37 °C in a humidified atmosphere containing 5% CO2. Cells were exposed for 48 h to nominal folate concentrations of 1, 100, 500, 750, or 1,000 μg/mL; the 1 μg/mL condition served as the reference control. This range overlaps the 1–1,000 μg/mL range examined in an earlier study of the same cell lines (5), but represents experimental culture exposure rather than a dietary dose. Cells were harvested, suspended, stained with trypan blue, and counted to assess viability and growth inhibition. Flow cytometry was used to assess cell-cycle distribution and apoptosis. The proliferation index was calculated as [(S + G2/M) / (G0/G1 + S + G2/M)] × 100%. The stated concentrations refer to nominal culture conditions, not measured intracellular concentrations.2.7Statistical analysisStatistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 24.0. Continuous variables were summarized as means ± standard deviations or medians with interquartile ranges (25th–75th percentiles). Analysis of variance was used for comparisons of continuous variables, and categorical variables were summarized as counts and percentages and compared using chi-square tests.The original Cox analysis assigned event time to the first scheduled follow-up visit at which persistence or progression was detected. This visit-based approximation does not identify the exact time of progression, which lies between histological assessments; persistence is a continuing baseline state rather than a newly occurring event. Accordingly, these hazard ratios require cautious interpretation and should not be read as estimates of a precisely observed onset of disease. Cox regression was used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs), adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs), and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). The adjusted model presented in Table 1 included erythrocyte folate, HR-HPV infection, and family history of tumors. Age, education, annual income, passive smoking, and menopausal status were considered potential confounders but are not included in that reported model. Low and high folate categories were defined using the cohort median of 347.49 ng/mL; this is a distribution-based threshold, not a diagnostic threshold for folate deficiency. Quartile comparisons used Q1 < 242.35, Q2 242.35 to <347.49, Q3 347.49 to <485.03, and Q4 ≥ 485.03 ng/mL, with Q4 as the reference. Restricted cubic spline models used four knots at the 5th, 35th, 65th, and 95th percentiles and a reference concentration of 347.49 ng/mL. Nonlinearity was assessed by jointly testing the second and third spline terms. ROC curves and AUCs described discrimination for the composite adverse outcome at each follow-up visit, both overall and within HR-HPV strata. Stratified associations were interpreted descriptively and were not taken as evidence of statistical interaction. Tests were two-sided, with a significance threshold of 0.05.Table 1Multivariable cox regression for the composite adverse CIN1 outcome.VariablesCategoryaHR (95% CI)p-valueErythrocyte folateLow (vs. High)2.42 (1.62, 3.61)<0.001HR-HPV infectionPositive (vs. Negative)2.08 (1.41, 3.07)<0.001Family history of tumorsYes (vs. No)1.15 (0.68, 1.95)0.599The reported model includes erythrocyte folate, HR-HPV infection, and family history of tumors. aHR, adjusted hazard ratio; CI, confidence interval. The composite outcome comprises persistence or progression to CIN2+. 3Results3.1Demographic characteristics of participantsThe 564 women with CIN1 were aged 19–65 years (mean, 49.28 ± 9.35 years). Most had a high school education or below (85.5%), were not farmers or workers (57.8%), were married (95.9%), and had an annual per capita income of ≤10,000 RMB (80.7%). full_text_sections.abstract: ObjectiveTo examine the association between baseline erythrocyte folate and reversal, persistence, and progression of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 1 (CIN1).MethodsThis community-based prospective cohort included 564 Chinese women with CIN1, with follow-up assessments at 6, 12, and 24 months. Baseline erythrocyte folate was measured by chemiluminescence immunoassay. Histological outcomes were classified as reversal, persistence, or progression to CIN2 or worse (CIN2+); persistence and progression formed a composite adverse outcome. Analyses included Cox regression, restricted cubic splines, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. Exploratory experiments assessed proliferation and apoptosis in C33A and CaSki cervical cancer cells.ResultsAmong the 453 women assessed at 24 months, 342 (75.5%) had reversal, 58 (12.8%) had persistence, and 53 (11.7%) had progression to CIN2+. Lower baseline erythrocyte folate was associated with the composite adverse outcome in the reported adjusted model (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] = 2.42, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.62–3.61). No statistically significant nonlinearity was detected for this outcome at 6 or 12 months (p = 0.655 and p = 0.127), whereas an L-shaped association was observed at 24 months (P for nonlinearity = 0.005). At 24 months, the area under the ROC curve (AUC) for folate was 0.703 (95% CI: 0.647–0.760) overall and 0.742 (95% CI: 0.646–0.837) within the high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV)-positive subgroup. Higher nominal folate concentrations reduced proliferation and increased apoptosis in the two cell lines.ConclusionLower baseline erythrocyte folate was associated with adverse CIN1 outcomes after adjustment for the covariates included in the reported model. Event-time assumptions and residual confounding limit interpretation. These findings do not establish causality, an interaction with HR-HPV, or a therapeutic benefit of folate supplementation. Prognostic use requires further validation.
full_text_sections.methods: 2Materials and methods2.1Study participantsParticipants were recruited from a community cohort established in two counties of Shanxi Province, China, using predefined eligibility criteria described previously (17). Of 39,971 women screened using the ThinPrep cytologic test (TCT), 37,219 had negative cytology and 2,752 had atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance or worse (ASC-US+). After excluding women with incomplete information (n = 387) or who declined follow-up (n = 68), 2,297 underwent HPV testing, colposcopy, and histological examination. Ten inadequate samples were excluded, leaving 2,287 women: 1,503 with a normal cervix (NC), 564 with CIN1, 218 with CIN2/3, and 2 with squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). The present analysis included the 564 women with CIN1 (Figure 1). The study was approved by the Ethics Committee of Shanxi Medical University (no. 2013-003), and all participants provided written informed consent.Figure 1Participant flow. Of 39,971 women screened, 37,219 had negative cytology and 2,752 had ASC-US+. After exclusion of 387 women with incomplete information and 68 who declined follow-up, 2,297 underwent further examination. Ten inadequate specimens were excluded, leaving 2,287 women with the diagnostic categories shown; the 564 women with CIN1 entered the present study. TCT, ThinPrep cytologic test; NILM, negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy; ASC-US+, atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance or worse; HPV, human papillomavirus; NC, normal cervix; CIN1, cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 1; CIN2/3, cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grades 2 or 3; SCC, squamous cell carcinoma.Flowchart showing participant selection for a study starting with 39,971 at baseline, divided into NILM (37,219) and ASC-UC+ (2,752). Exclusions and follow-up processes result in enrollment of subgroups NC (1,503), CIN1 (564), CIN2/3 (218), and SCC (2) into the present study.2.2Data and sample collectionTrained investigators conducted face-to-face interviews using a standardized questionnaire to collect demographic characteristics, lifestyle factors, personal hygiene practices, menstrual and sexual history, and family history of tumors. A 2 mL venous blood sample was collected in an anticoagulant tube for erythrocyte folate measurement. Exfoliated cervical cells were collected for HPV typing. Samples were stored at −80 °C. HPV genotyping and erythrocyte folate measurement were performed within 2 and 5 days, respectively.2.3Definition of exposure and outcomeWomen with CIN1 at baseline were scheduled for histological follow-up at 6, 12, and 24 months. Baseline erythrocyte folate concentration defined the exposure. At each visit, histology was compared with baseline: NC was classified as reversal, CIN1 as persistence, and CIN2 + as progression. Persistence and progression were combined as a composite adverse outcome for selected analyses, while their separate frequencies and associations were also reported because they differ in clinical significance. CIN2 + denotes CIN2 or worse and should not be interpreted as invasive cancer alone. Women diagnosed with CIN2 + received treatment according to clinical guidelines (18). Visit-specific outcome proportions were calculated among women assessed at the corresponding visit.2.4Detection of erythrocyte folateErythrocyte folate was measured by chemiluminescence immunoassay using a folate assay kit (Beckman Coulter, United States) according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Hematocrit was measured, and blood samples were hemolyzed before folate measurement against a calibration curve. The reported calculation was: erythrocyte folate (ng/mL) = [folate concentration in the hemolysate (ng/mL) × dilution factor] / [hematocrit (%) / 100].2.5HPV detection and typingExfoliated cervical cells were processed for HPV DNA extraction and flow-through hybridization using a kit from Chaozhou Kaipu Biochemical Company, China. The assay identified 15 high-risk and 6 low-risk HPV types, as described previously (17). Detection of any high-risk type was classified as HR-HPV positive; absence of the assayed high-risk types was classified as HR-HPV negative.2.6Exploratory cell culture and folate exposureHPV-negative C33A and HPV-positive CaSki cervical cancer cell lines (Academy of Medical Sciences, China) were cultured in MEM-EBSS and RPMI-1640 medium, respectively, supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum and penicillin–streptomycin. Cells were maintained at 37 °C in a humidified atmosphere containing 5% CO2. Cells were exposed for 48 h to nominal folate concentrations of 1, 100, 500, 750, or 1,000 μg/mL; the 1 μg/mL condition served as the reference control. This range overlaps the 1–1,000 μg/mL range examined in an earlier study of the same cell lines (5), but represents experimental culture exposure rather than a dietary dose. Cells were harvested, suspended, stained with trypan blue, and counted to assess viability and growth inhibition. Flow cytometry was used to assess cell-cycle distribution and apoptosis. The proliferation index was calculated as [(S + G2/M) / (G0/G1 + S + G2/M)] × 100%. The stated concentrations refer to nominal culture conditions, not measured intracellular concentrations.2.7Statistical analysisStatistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 24.0. Continuous variables were summarized as means ± standard deviations or medians with interquartile ranges (25th–75th percentiles). Analysis of variance was used for comparisons of continuous variables, and categorical variables were summarized as counts and percentages and compared using chi-square tests.The original Cox analysis assigned event time to the first scheduled follow-up visit at which persistence or progression was detected. This visit-based approximation does not identify the exact time of progression, which lies between histological assessments; persistence is a continuing baseline state rather than a newly occurring event. Accordingly, these hazard ratios require cautious interpretation and should not be read as estimates of a precisely observed onset of disease. Cox regression was used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs), adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs), and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). The adjusted model presented in Table 1 included erythrocyte folate, HR-HPV infection, and family history of tumors. Age, education, annual income, passive smoking, and menopausal status were considered potential confounders but are not included in that reported model. Low and high folate categories were defined using the cohort median of 347.49 ng/mL; this is a distribution-based threshold, not a diagnostic threshold for folate deficiency. Quartile comparisons used Q1 < 242.35, Q2 242.35 to <347.49, Q3 347.49 to <485.03, and Q4 ≥ 485.03 ng/mL, with Q4 as the reference. Restricted cubic spline models used four knots at the 5th, 35th, 65th, and 95th percentiles and a reference concentration of 347.49 ng/mL. Nonlinearity was assessed by jointly testing the second and third spline terms. ROC curves and AUCs described discrimination for the composite adverse outcome at each follow-up visit, both overall and within HR-HPV strata. Stratified associations were interpreted descriptively and were not taken as evidence of statistical interaction. Tests were two-sided, with a significance threshold of 0.05.Table 1Multivariable cox regression for the composite adverse CIN1 outcome.VariablesCategoryaHR (95% CI)p-valueErythrocyte folateLow (vs. High)2.42 (1.62, 3.61)<0.001HR-HPV infectionPositive (vs. Negative)2.08 (1.41, 3.07)<0.001Family history of tumorsYes (vs. No)1.15 (0.68, 1.95)0.599The reported model includes erythrocyte folate, HR-HPV infection, and family history of tumors. aHR, adjusted hazard ratio; CI, confidence interval. The composite outcome comprises persistence or progression to CIN2+.

full_text_sections.discussion: 4DiscussionThis prospective cohort identified an association between lower baseline erythrocyte folate and adverse CIN1 outcomes after adjustment for HR-HPV infection and family history of tumors in the reported model. Most women assessed at 24 months had reversal, while 12.8% had persistence and 11.7% had progression to CIN2+. Comparisons with other cohorts, including a Japanese cohort (19), should account for differences in participant characteristics, follow-up, and outcome definitions; our data do not establish that dietary differences explain variation between studies. For the composite adverse outcome, nonlinearity was not statistically significant at 6 or 12 months, whereas a significant nonlinear, L-shaped pattern was observed at 24 months. This time-specific finding argues against a single overall L-shaped relationship or a clinically established folate threshold.Folate participates in nucleotide synthesis and methyl-group metabolism (20, 21). Earlier studies have linked folate status to altered methylation and expression of FHIT and cervical cancer-related microRNAs (5, 9, 22), while homocysteine and LINE-1 methylation have also been associated with high-grade cervical lesions (23). These findings suggest biological pathways worth testing. However, the present study did not measure DNA methylation, HPV integration, or these molecular mediators. The observed cohort association and cellular growth responses therefore cannot establish a specific pathway connecting erythrocyte folate with CIN1 outcomes.The AUC of 0.703 for folate alone indicates modest within-cohort discrimination and should not be characterized as evidence of a clinically validated prognostic test. HPV status is associated with the natural history of CIN1 (24), and other studies have investigated HPV DNA load with p16/Ki-67 staining and CK7 immunohistochemistry (25, 26). We did not directly compare folate against these markers and cannot claim superiority. Prior work has examined serum folate together with HR-HPV in CIN1 prognosis (27), but this does not substitute for an interaction test in the current cohort. Before clinical use, folate-based models require assessment of calibration, discrimination, optimism through internal validation, external performance, and clinical utility beyond established predictors. In a different disease setting, Filippini et al. similarly concluded that promising HPV circulating tumor DNA findings in head and neck cancer require prospective interventional evidence before biomarker-guided decisions can be adopted routinely (28). That review provides a general validation perspective, not direct evidence for folate in CIN1.The cell experiments showed reduced proliferation and increased apoptosis at higher nominal folate concentrations in C33A and CaSki cells. C33A and CaSki are established cervical cancer lines, not primary CIN1 epithelial cells; their responses cannot confirm a mechanism for the cohort association or a clinical benefit for CIN1. The absence of a statistically significant difference between one HPV-negative and one HPV-positive line also does not establish HPV-independent effects, because the lines differ in other biological characteristics. Earlier work in these cell lines used folate concentrations of 1–1,000 μg/mL (5), whereas a separate study reported responses at 200 and 500 nM in HeLa and SiHa cells (9). These different exposure ranges and cellular contexts are not directly interchangeable. Folate deprivation has also induced apoptosis in HepG2 cells (29), illustrating that findings depend on the model and exposure conditions rather than supporting a universal direction of effect. Experiments in CIN1-derived epithelial cultures or relevant organoids would be needed to address lesion-specific biology.Clinical interpretation also requires distinguishing culture exposure from dietary intake. Under the US National Academies framework summarized by the National Institutes of Health, the recommended intake for nonpregnant adults is 400 μg dietary folate equivalents (DFE)/day; pregnancy and lactation recommendations are 600 and 500 μg DFE/day, respectively. The adult tolerable upper intake level is 1,000 μg/day of folic acid from supplements and fortified foods, excluding naturally occurring food folate and medically supervised treatment (30). This upper limit is not a treatment target. The 5 mg/day regimens used in cervical lesion trials (15, 16) exceed the general adult upper limit and should not be translated into routine supplementation advice. Our nominal culture concentrations of 1–1,000 μg/mL cannot be converted into an oral dose or used to define a safe intake. The cohort median is also not a diagnostic deficiency threshold. The present findings therefore support further clinical investigation rather than a recommendation for high-dose folic acid to treat CIN1.The prospective design and repeated histological assessments are strengths, but several limitations constrain interpretation. Folate was measured only at baseline, so changes in exposure could not be assessed. Follow-up fell to 80.32% at 24 months, creating potential selection bias if missingness was related to folate or outcomes. Adjustment in the reported model was limited to HR-HPV infection and family history of tumors; residual confounding by age, socioeconomic factors, smoking exposure, menopausal status, and other determinants remains possible. Progression was detected only at scheduled visits, making its timing interval-censored. In addition, persistence is a baseline state, so treating its first follow-up detection as an incident event complicates the interpretation of the composite Cox endpoint. Analysis of visit-specific outcomes and sensitivity analyses that account for interval-censored progression are needed to assess robustness. No external validation of the prognostic estimates is available, and formal interaction evidence is required before claiming effect modification. The cancer cell experiments were exploratory, and nominal culture concentrations cannot substitute for measurements of extracellular or intracellular folate. Neither the observational cohort nor these experiments establish a causal or therapeutic effect in CIN1.These findings support further investigation of erythrocyte folate as a candidate prognostic marker. Future studies should use clearly defined progression and persistence endpoints, repeated folate measurements, broader confounder control, and independent validation. Randomized studies with clinically appropriate doses and safety monitoring are needed to determine whether folate supplementation changes CIN1 outcomes.
full_text_sections.conclusion: 5ConclusionLower baseline erythrocyte folate was associated with adverse CIN1 outcomes after adjustment for HR-HPV infection and family history of tumors in the reported model. The dose–response pattern varied by follow-up duration, and discrimination was modest within this cohort. These findings do not establish causality, statistical interaction with HR-HPV, or a therapeutic benefit of supplementation. The C33A and CaSki experiments provide exploratory evidence on cancer cell responses and do not directly model CIN1. Further methodological assessment, validation, and intervention studies are required before clinical application.
full_text_sections.other: 1IntroductionCervical cancer remains a major public health concern. The GLOBOCAN 2020 estimates included approximately 604,000 new cases and 342,000 deaths worldwide (1), and national registry data also document a substantial burden in China (2). Population-based research in Shanxi Province has examined factors associated with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (3). CIN1 is a low-grade lesion that may regress, persist, or progress to CIN2+. Its natural history varies across populations, including women living with human immunodeficiency virus (4). Identifying factors associated with these distinct outcomes may improve understanding of CIN1 prognosis; persistence should not be equated with malignant transformation.Persistent infection with oncogenic human papillomavirus (HPV) is central to cervical carcinogenesis, but infection alone does not explain variation in lesion outcomes. Folate supports nucleotide synthesis and one-carbon metabolism, including the supply of methyl groups for DNA methylation (5, 6). Folate-related changes in DNA integrity and methylation provide biological hypotheses for an association with cervical lesions. The folate-sensitive fragile site FRA3B overlaps a documented HPV16 integration site (7, 8), although this observation does not demonstrate that low folate causes viral integration in women with CIN1. Studies in cervical tissues and cancer cells have linked folate status to fragile histidine triad (FHIT) methylation and expression (5), and to microRNA-27a-3p expression and cellular proliferation and invasion (9). These findings provide a rationale for prospective investigation rather than proof of a mechanism governing CIN1 outcomes.Observational studies have associated folate status with cervical cytological abnormalities (10), and have examined dietary and circulating folate in relation to cervical neoplasia (11). Our previous population-based studies identified associations of serum or erythrocyte folate with cervical lesions and HR-HPV infection (12, 13). Experimental work has also linked folate availability to DNA methyltransferase 1 expression and cervical cancer cell behavior (14). Evidence from intervention studies is mixed: one trial reported greater CIN1 regression with 5 mg/day of folate for 6 months (15), whereas a larger trial using 5 mg/day of folic acid in women with early cervical abnormalities found no significant improvement in regression (16). Differences in populations and endpoints limit direct comparison. Prospective evidence on baseline erythrocyte folate and subsequent CIN1 outcomes remains limited. We therefore examined its associations with reversal, persistence, and progression in a community-based cohort.We also conducted exploratory in vitro experiments to characterize proliferation, cell-cycle distribution, and apoptosis after folate exposure in C33A and CaSki cervical cancer cells. These experiments were not designed to model CIN1 directly or to establish a mechanism for the cohort associations. 2.1Study participantsParticipants were recruited from a community cohort established in two counties of Shanxi Province, China, using predefined eligibility criteria described previously (17). Of 39,971 women screened using the ThinPrep cytologic test (TCT), 37,219 had negative cytology and 2,752 had atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance or worse (ASC-US+). After excluding women with incomplete information (n = 387) or who declined follow-up (n = 68), 2,297 underwent HPV testing, colposcopy, and histological examination. Ten inadequate samples were excluded, leaving 2,287 women: 1,503 with a normal cervix (NC), 564 with CIN1, 218 with CIN2/3, and 2 with squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). The present analysis included the 564 women with CIN1 (Figure 1). The study was approved by the Ethics Committee of Shanxi Medical University (no. 2013-003), and all participants provided written informed consent.Figure 1Participant flow. Of 39,971 women screened, 37,219 had negative cytology and 2,752 had ASC-US+. After exclusion of 387 women with incomplete information and 68 who declined follow-up, 2,297 underwent further examination. Ten inadequate specimens were excluded, leaving 2,287 women with the diagnostic categories shown; the 564 women with CIN1 entered the present study. TCT, ThinPrep cytologic test; NILM, negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy; ASC-US+, atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance or worse; HPV, human papillomavirus; NC, normal cervix; CIN1, cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 1; CIN2/3, cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grades 2 or 3; SCC, squamous cell carcinoma.Flowchart showing participant selection for a study starting with 39,971 at baseline, divided into NILM (37,219) and ASC-UC+ (2,752). Exclusions and follow-up processes result in enrollment of subgroups NC (1,503), CIN1 (564), CIN2/3 (218), and SCC (2) into the present study. 2.2Data and sample collectionTrained investigators conducted face-to-face interviews using a standardized questionnaire to collect demographic characteristics, lifestyle factors, personal hygiene practices, menstrual and sexual history, and family history of tumors. A 2 mL venous blood sample was collected in an anticoagulant tube for erythrocyte folate measurement. Exfoliated cervical cells were collected for HPV typing. Samples were stored at −80 °C. HPV genotyping and erythrocyte folate measurement were performed within 2 and 5 days, respectively. 2.3Definition of exposure and outcomeWomen with CIN1 at baseline were scheduled for histological follow-up at 6, 12, and 24 months. Baseline erythrocyte folate concentration defined the exposure. At each visit, histology was compared with baseline: NC was classified as reversal, CIN1 as persistence, and CIN2 + as progression. Persistence and progression were combined as a composite adverse outcome for selected analyses, while their separate frequencies and associations were also reported because they differ in clinical significance. CIN2 + denotes CIN2 or worse and should not be interpreted as invasive cancer alone. Women diagnosed with CIN2 + received treatment according to clinical guidelines (18). Visit-specific outcome proportions were calculated among women assessed at the corresponding visit. 2.4Detection of erythrocyte folateErythrocyte folate was measured by chemiluminescence immunoassay using a folate assay kit (Beckman Coulter, United States) according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Hematocrit was measured, and blood samples were hemolyzed before folate measurement against a calibration curve. The reported calculation was: erythrocyte folate (ng/mL) = [folate concentration in the hemolysate (ng/mL) × dilution factor] / [hematocrit (%) / 100]. 2.5HPV detection and typingExfoliated cervical cells were processed for HPV DNA extraction and flow-through hybridization using a kit from Chaozhou Kaipu Biochemical Company, China. The assay identified 15 high-risk and 6 low-risk HPV types, as described previously (17). Detection of any high-risk type was classified as HR-HPV positive; absence of the assayed high-risk types was classified as HR-HPV negative. 2.6Exploratory cell culture and folate exposureHPV-negative C33A and HPV-positive CaSki cervical cancer cell lines (Academy of Medical Sciences, China) were cultured in MEM-EBSS and RPMI-1640 medium, respectively, supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum and penicillin–streptomycin. Cells were maintained at 37 °C in a humidified atmosphere containing 5% CO2. Cells were exposed for 48 h to nominal folate concentrations of 1, 100, 500, 750, or 1,000 μg/mL; the 1 μg/mL condition served as the reference control. This range overlaps the 1–1,000 μg/mL range examined in an earlier study of the same cell lines (5), but represents experimental culture exposure rather than a dietary dose. title_original: Baseline erythrocyte folate and outcomes of low grade cervical intraepithelial neoplasia in a prospective cohort

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the association between baseline erythrocyte folate levels and outcomes of low-grade cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN1) in a prospective cohort. The research addressed the knowledge gap regarding the impact of folate on CIN1 progression and provided a rationale for understanding nutritional factors in cervical cancer prevention.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A prospective cohort study was conducted from 2020 to 2024, enrolling 1,503 women with no cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (NC), 564 with CIN1, 218 with CIN2/3, and 2 with squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). Data were collected through face-to-face interviews and erythrocyte folate levels were measured using chemiluminescence immunoassay.
analysis.methods: Erythrocyte folate levels were measured using a chemiluminescence immunoassay. Cox regression, restricted cubic splines, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were used for statistical analyses. The study adjusted for potential confounders such as HR-HPV infection and family history of tumors.
analysis.main_results: Lower baseline erythrocyte folate was associated with adverse CIN1 outcomes, with an adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) of 2.42 (95% CI: 1.62–3.61). No significant nonlinearity was detected at 6 or 12 months, but an L-shaped association was observed at 24 months (P for nonlinearity = 0.005).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that lower baseline erythrocyte folate was associated with adverse CIN1 outcomes after adjustment for confounders. This association was novel and provided insights into the role of folate in CIN1 progression.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that maintaining adequate folate levels may be beneficial in preventing adverse outcomes of CIN1. This could inform surveillance and prevention strategies for cervical cancer.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include event-time assumptions and residual confounding, which limit the interpretation of the results. The evidence strength is moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: A prospective cohort study found that lower baseline erythrocyte folate levels were associated with adverse outcomes of CIN1, with an adjusted hazard ratio of 2.42. This study provides novel insights into the role of folate in CIN1 progression and suggests potential benefits of maintaining adequate folate levels for cervical cancer prevention.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在通过前瞻性 队列研究 调查基线红细胞叶酸水平与低度宫颈上皮内瘤变 (CIN1) 结局之间的关联。该研究解决了有关叶酸对 CIN1 进展影响的知识差距,并为了解 宫颈癌 预防中的营养因素提供了理论基础。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项前瞻性 队列研究 研究于 2020 年至 2024 年进行,招募了 1,503 名无宫颈上皮内瘤变 (NC) 的女性、564 名患有 CIN1 的女性、218 名患有 CIN2/3 的女性和 2 名患有鳞状细胞癌 (SCC) 的女性。通过面对面访谈收集数据,并使用化学发光免疫测定法测量红细胞叶酸水平。
elements_zh.methods: 使用化学发光免疫测定法测量红细胞叶酸水平。Cox 回归、限制三次样条和受试者工作特征 (ROC) 曲线用于统计分析。该研究调整了潜在的混杂因素,例如 HR-HPV 感染和肿瘤家族史。
elements_zh.main_results: 较低的基线红细胞叶酸与不良 CIN1 结局相关,调整后的风险比 (aHR) 为 2.42 (95% CI: 1.62–3.61)。在 6 个月或 12 个月时未检测到显着的非线性,但在 24 个月时观察到 L 形关联(非线性 P = 0.005)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究发现,调整混杂因素后,较低的红细胞叶酸基线与不良 CIN1 结局相关。这种关联是新颖的,并为了解叶酸在 CIN1 进展中的作用提供了见解。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,维持足够的叶酸水平可能有益于预防 CIN1 的不良后果。这可以为 监测 和 宫颈癌 的预防策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性包括事件时间假设和残留混杂因素,这限制了结果的解释。由于这些限制,证据强度中等。

analysis_zh.main_results: 较低的基线红细胞叶酸与不良 CIN1 结局相关,调整后的风险比 (aHR) 为 2.42 (95% CI: 1.62–3.61)。在 6 个月或 12 个月时未检测到显着的非线性,但在 24 个月时观察到 L 形关联(非线性 P = 0.005)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究发现,调整混杂因素后,较低的红细胞叶酸基线与不良 CIN1 结局相关。这种关联是新颖的,并为了解叶酸在 CIN1 进展中的作用提供了见解。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,维持足够的叶酸水平可能有益于预防 CIN1 的不良后果。这可以为 监测 和 宫颈癌 的预防策略提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性包括事件时间假设和残留混杂因素,这限制了结果的解释。由于这些限制,证据强度中等。

full_text: Abstract Background Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) is a major etiological basis for cervical cancer and several other epithelial malignancies. In-depth dissection of early HPV entry and intracellular trafficking is therefore important for identifying novel targets for blocking HPV infection. Main body HPV entry is not a linear process mediated by a single receptor, but a multistep trafficking network spanning the basement membrane (BM)/extracellular matrix (ECM), plasma membrane, endosomes, Golgi-related compartments and nucleus. In the relatively well-characterized HPV16 and pseudovirion (PsV)-based models, HPV virions can be captured and initially attached by BM/ECM-associated and cell-surface attachment factors, including laminin-332 (LN332) and heparan sulfate proteoglycans (HSPGs). Subsequently, host factors such as cyclophilin B (CyPB) and furin participate in capsid conformational priming, L2 N-terminal exposure, and furin-mediated L2 cleavage, thereby creating conditions for the transition of virions from initial attachment to entry platform assembly. Integrin/focal adhesion kinase (FAK) signaling, tetraspanin-enriched microdomains (TEMs), the annexin A2/S100A10 heterotetramer (A2t), and cytoskeleton-associated regulators have been implicated in entry platform organization, atypical endocytosis, and early intracellular trafficking, although their points of action and degrees of dependence may vary with HPV type, cell model, and experimental system. After entry into the endosomal system, γ-secretase-mediated L2 membrane insertion, Retromer/Retriever-mediated retrograde trafficking, and vesicle-enclosed, mitosis-dependent nuclear entry are thought to promote delivery of the L2/viral DNA (vDNA) complex to the nucleus. Short conclusion This review summarizes the key host factors, membrane platforms, atypical endocytic routes, endosomal sorting events, retrograde trafficking pathways, and nuclear entry processes involved in HPV entry, and discusses their potential value as early intervention targets against HPV infection. analysis.methods: The review summarized the key host factors, membrane platforms, atypical endocytic routes, endosomal sorting events, retrograde trafficking pathways, and nuclear entry processes involved in HPV entry, using a combination of literature review and experimental data.
analysis.main_results: The review detailed the multistep trafficking network of HPV entry, including initial attachment by BM/ECM-associated and cell-surface attachment factors, capsid conformational priming, L2 N-terminal exposure, and furin-mediated L2 cleavage, followed by entry platform organization and intracellular trafficking events.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as highlighting the potential value of key host factors and intracellular trafficking processes as early intervention targets against HPV infection, emphasizing the complexity of HPV entry and the need for further research.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment strategies for HPV-associated diseases, particularly cervical cancer, by identifying novel targets for intervention.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on a review of existing literature and experimental data, which may not capture all nuances of HPV entry in different contexts. The evidence strength is moderate due to the lack of original experimental data.

analysis.summary_en: This review summarizes the molecular mechanisms of human papillomavirus (HPV) entry and intracellular trafficking, highlighting key host factors and intracellular processes as potential targets for intervention against HPV infection, which is a major cause of cervical cancer and other epithelial malignancies.

full_text: Abstract Persistent oncogenic human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is the major cause of cervical dysplasia and cervical carcinoma, although its association with marital status remains inconsistent. This exploratory cross-sectional study examined the association between marital status and HPV 16/18 E6/E7 oncoprotein positivity and cervical dysplasia among women screened in Lafia, Nigeria. A minimum sample size of 52 was calculated using Cochran's formula, based on an HPV 16/18 prevalence of 3.5%. However, 75 women aged ≥18 years were consecutively recruited and screened using visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA), Pap smear cytology, and an HPV 16/18 rapid test. Marital status was recorded in four categories but dichotomised as ever-married versus never-married because of the sparse outcome events. Cervical dysplasia was diagnosed in 8/75 women (10.7%), while HPV 16/18 positivity was detected in 9/75 women (12.0%). Marital status was not significantly associated with either outcome (cervical dysplasia: OR = 1.69, 95% CI: 0.19 to 14.92; HPV 16/18 positivity: OR = 0.78, 95% CI: 0.14 to 4.22; p = 1.00 and p = 0.67, respectively). HPV 16/18 positivity was associated with cervical dysplasia (37.5% vs. 9.0%; OR = 6.10, 95% CI: 1.16 to 32.05; p = 0.050). The study found no statistically significant association between marital status and either outcome, whereas HPV 16/18 positivity was associated with cervical dysplasia. Larger, adequately powered studies are needed to establish whether marital status has any role in cervical cancer risk stratification. full_text: - Page Path HOME > Epidemiol Health > Accepted Articles > Article - Cohort profile Cohort profile: the National Human Papillomavirus Immunization Program Cohort in Korea Jinhee Lee1,2 , Hee-Yeon Kang1 , Hyunju Lee3 , Kyung-Jin Min4 , Jeeyeon Shin5 , Boyeong Ryu5 , Eunjin Hyun5 , Hoyeon Jang6 , Log Young Kim6 , Jaiyong Kim6 , Jin-Kyoung Oh1 Epidemiol Health 2026;e2026068 DOI: https://doi.org/10.4178/epih.e2026068 [Accepted] Published online: November 25, 2026 1Department of Public Health & AI, Graduate School of Cancer Science and Policy, National Cancer Center, Goyang, Korea 2Program in Public Health, Korea University Graduate School, Seoul, Korea 33Department of Pediatrics, Seoul National University Bundang Hospital, Seoul National University College of Medicine, Seongnam, Korea 4Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, Korea University Ansan Hospital, Korea University College of Medicine, Ansan, Korea 5Division of Immunization Services, Department of Healthcare Safety and Immunization, Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency, Cheongju, Korea 6Department of Big Data Management, National Health Insurance Service, Wonju, Korea Corresponding author: Jin-Kyoung Oh, Email: jkoh@ncc.re.kr Received: 17 August 2026 â¢ Revised: 17 October 2026 â¢ Accepted: 4 November 2026 - 50 Views - 0 Download - 0 Crossref - 0 Scopus Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination effectively prevents HPV-related diseases, including anogenital warts, cervical cancer, and other HPV-associated cancers. In 2016, the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency (KDCA) added HPV vaccination to the National Immunization Program (NIP), initially targeting 12-year-old girls. As the vaccinated population matures, evaluating the long-term effectiveness of the national vaccination program is becoming increasingly important. We therefore established the Korean HPV NIP cohort by linking the KDCA Immunization Registry Information System with the National Health Information Database of the National Health Insurance Service (NHIS-NHID). The cohort includes 2,251,563 girls born between 2003 and 2012 who were identified in the NHIS-NHID. Vaccination status was classified by vaccine type and number of doses received. Incident HPV-related diseases were identified from International Classification of Diseases, 10th revision, codes recorded as primary diagnoses in health insurance claims. The Korean HPV NIP cohort provides a nationwide, population-based resource for longitudinal monitoring of HPV-related disease incidence and evaluation of vaccine effectiveness. As follow-up data accumulate, the cohort will support assessments of vaccine effectiveness against a broad spectrum of HPV-related outcomes and inform future HPV vaccination policy.

title_original: Cohort profile: the National Human Papillomavirus Immunization Program Cohort in Korea

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to establish a cohort to evaluate the long-term effectiveness of the national HPV vaccination program in Korea, addressing the need to monitor the incidence of HPV-related diseases as the vaccinated population matures.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The Korean HPV NIP cohort was established by linking the KDCA Immunization Registry Information System with the NHIS-NHID, including 2,251,563 girls born between 2003 and 2012, to evaluate vaccine effectiveness and support future policy decisions.
analysis.methods: Vaccination status was classified by vaccine type and number of doses received, and incident HPV-related diseases were identified from health insurance claims using ICD-10 codes.
analysis.main_results: The cohort provides a nationwide, population-based resource for longitudinal monitoring of HPV-related disease incidence and evaluation of vaccine effectiveness.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The cohort will support assessments of vaccine effectiveness against a broad spectrum of HPV-related outcomes and inform future HPV vaccination policy.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The cohort will help in evaluating the long-term effectiveness of the national HPV vaccination program and inform future policy decisions regarding HPV vaccination.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the reliance on claims data for disease identification and the potential for unmeasured confounders, but it provides a valuable resource for evaluating vaccine effectiveness.

analysis.summary_en: This study established a nationwide cohort to evaluate the long-term effectiveness of the national HPV vaccination program in Korea, providing a resource for monitoring HPV-related diseases and informing future policy decisions.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在建立 队列研究 来评估韩国国家 HPV 疫苗接种 计划的长期有效性,解决随着疫苗接种人群成熟而监测 HPV 相关疾病 发病率 的需要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 韩国 HPV NIP 队列研究 是通过将 KDCA 免疫登记信息系统与 NHIS-NHID 连接而建立的,其中包括 2003 年至 2012 年间出生的 2,251,563 名女孩,以评估 疫苗 的有效性并支持未来的政策决策。
elements_zh.methods: 疫苗接种 状态按 疫苗 类型和接受的剂量次数进行分类,并使用 ICD-10 代码从健康保险索赔中识别出与 HPV 相关的疾病事件。
elements_zh.main_results: 队列研究 提供了全国性的、以人群为基础的资源,用于纵向监测 HPV 相关疾病 发病率 和评估 疫苗 的有效性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 队列研究 将支持针对广泛的 HPV 相关结果评估 疫苗 的有效性,并为未来的 HPV 疫苗接种 政策提供信息。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 队列研究 将有助于评估国家 HPV 疫苗接种 计划的长期有效性,并为未来有关 HPV 疫苗接种 的政策决策提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因疾病识别对索赔数据的依赖以及可能存在未测量的混杂因素而受到限制,但它为评估 疫苗 的有效性提供了宝贵的资源。
